1|# AUDIT.md — Multi-project production-readiness audit
2|
3|Task: `5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085` — review the multi-project
4|mechanisms to confirm KainBain can handle production-level workloads across
5|multiple projects at once (untested since runners were implemented).
6|
7|Guidance: [FRAMEWORKS.md](./FRAMEWORKS.md) (ISO 25010 spine, 29119 tests, SRE
8|bar, Twelve-Factor runner lifecycle, named queue patterns, ASVS V4/V5).
9|Survey inputs: [INTENT-SURVEY.md](./INTENT-SURVEY.md),
10|[FEEDBACK_SURVEY.md](./FEEDBACK_SURVEY.md).
11|
12|## 0. Survey responses — disposition
13|
14|Both survey files were read. Their `answers` blocks are empty (no operator
15|selections recorded), so per the survey's own "Auditor's choice / judgement
16|call" options this audit proceeds on auditor's judgement with these
17|recorded interpretations (each maps to one FEEDBACK_SURVEY question):
18|
19|| Survey Q | Interpretation used |
20||---|---|
21|| q1 queue model | Pass = one shared central queue drained in central-queue order, OR per-project queues with a shared pool + documented fairness — whichever exists must show no silos, no unbounded starvation, no silent drops. (Found: the former.) |
22|| q2 load/unload | Pass = drain-and-fence semantics: in-flight work finishes or is safely parked, no new claims after unload, re-load resumes cleanly. Hard-detach or restart-required unload would be a hitch/blocker. |
23|| q3 switch + interleave | All four guarantees required: switch never interrupts others; one runner interleaves with correct projectId; cross-project writes rejected; git/workdir isolation holds. |
24|| q4 skills | All four behaviours required: merge-not-replace; per-project-only shadowing; project-agnostic core skills; invalid/oversized never crashes a stage. |
25|| q5 hard-coding | True `kainbain`-as-project assumptions = blocker. Benign strings (product name, sample data, fallbacks) = observation with disposition. |
26|| q6 synthetic testing | Ephemeral temp-dir fixtures with auto-cleanup + contamination checks (live dummy projects read-only, never mutated, none added). |
27|| q7/q8 scale bar | Auditor's judgement: no full load rig in this stage; small-scale bar (2–3 projects, 1–2 runners) judged on code + unit/integration evidence, full production-scale SLO gate left explicitly open with a proposed SLO set. |
28|
29|## 1. Verdict
30|
31|**READY WITH HITCHES for small-scale multi-project use (2–3 concurrent
32|projects, 1–2 runners) — the "start developing apps" goal. NOT YET PROVEN at
33|production scale: the SRE SLO gate (FRAMEWORKS §6) is open.**
34|
35|- Zero blockers found in Q1–Q7. Every must-have mechanism exists, is wired,
36|  and is covered by passing tests re-run in this audit (187 tests green).
37|- Five hitches (H-1…H-5) and three observations (O-1…O-3) are recorded below
38|  with owners' next actions. None stops app-development use.
39|- Q8 is `not yet measurable` per SRE Ch.3 (no declared SLOs, no load/soak or
40|  failure drills executed here). §7 proposes the SLO set and the drill list
41|  that closes the gate. Do not claim production-scale readiness until that
42|  gate is run.
43|
44|## 2. Per-check results
45|
46|### Q1 — Switch projects without interrupting others — PASS
47|
48|Switching is a view-layer id flip with no execution coupling:
49|
50|- Backend: `POST /projects/:id/activate` → `projectStore.setActiveProject`
51|  ([projects.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/api/routes/projects.js) ~L612).
52|  It only sets `activeProjectId`; no task, claim, scheduler, or runner state
53|  is touched.
54|- Dispatch (`scanClaimableTasks`,
55|  [scanClaimableTasks.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/api/flow/dispatch/scanClaimableTasks.js))
56|  and the embedded scheduler
57|  ([findNextCandidateTask.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/api/flow/scheduler/findNextCandidateTask.js))
58|  iterate `projectStore.listProjects()` — all projects, never the active one.
59|- The runner daemon never reads the active project; every call carries an
60|  explicit `projectId` ([client.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/runner/client.js)).
61|- The multi-runner monitor resolves each hold from the held task's own
62|  project, "never from whatever pipeline the viewer has selected"
63|  ([runnerRoutes.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/api/flow/runnerRoutes.js) ~L523).
64|- Worktree bulkhead: per-workdir promise chains (`workdirChains`,
65|  [project.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/runner/project.js))
66|  serialize git per workdir, and stale-lock recovery refuses to act while a
67|  live git process runs — one wedged project cannot stall another's git.
68|
69|Hitch H-1 (see §3): runner-mutating endpoints resolve a *missing* projectId
70|to the active project instead of rejecting (fail-open default tenant).
71|
72|### Q2 — Multiple projects collapse to one queue — PASS
73|
74|One shared central queue, not per-project silos:
75|
76|- `scanClaimableTasks` scans every project (allowlist-filtered only by the
77|  runner's own `projectIds`) and sorts through the single shared seam
78|  `sortCentralQueue`, used identically by runner dispatch, the embedded
79|  scheduler, and the queue display — the three can never disagree about
80|  "what runs next".
81|- Order: oldest-waiting-first globally, furthest-along percentage tiebreak,
82|  15-minute starvation ceiling (overdue jumps ahead oldest-first)
83|  ([centralQueuePolicy.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/api/flow/scheduler/centralQueuePolicy.js)).
84|- Contention safety: the claim fence (`ClaimStore.claim`, `CLAIM_CONFLICT`
85|  on lost races) is the single arbiter; concurrent loops poll again rather
86|  than double-dispatch. `noDoubleDispatch.test.js` passes.
87|- Backpressure: fleet-wide cap → HTTP 429 `FLEET_CONCURRENCY_EXHAUSTED`
88|  (daemon backs off *without* consuming idle budget); per-project cap skips
89|  that project's candidates (`PROJECT_BUSY`) instead of blocking the queue.
90|- Tests re-run green: `scanClaimableTasks.test.js` (6),
91|  `centralQueueFairness.test.js` (7), `runnerDispatchCaps.test.js`,
92|  `runnerPolicyDispatch.test.js`, `noDoubleDispatch.test.js`.
93|
94|Hitch H-2: fairness is FIFO-only with no per-project quota — a sustained
95|burst from one project delays others up to the ceiling. Documented tradeoff,
96|not a correctness failure.
97|
98|### Q3 — Projects loaded/unloaded from runners — PASS WITH HITCH
99|
100|Load/unload *from runners* works with drain-and-fence semantics and no
101|restart on the operator path:
102|
103|- Load: `POST /projects/register` → idempotent `registerProjectPath`
104|  (re-register is a no-op) + `ProjectStore` rescan; registry file is
105|  advisory (missing/corrupt → empty, never broken boot).
106|- Runner-side scope: `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_PROJECTS` allowlist, sent on every
107|  `dispatchClaim` poll; empty = serve all.
108|- Operator-side unload at runtime: `PATCH /runners/:id/config`
109|  `{ projectScope: [...] }` (persisted, no restart), enforced on dispatch,
110|  direct claim, and merge-lease paths by the single point
111|  `operatorConfigVerdict` → loud `PROJECT_SCOPE` refusal, never silent skip.
112|- In-flight work drains: scope changes touch only future matching — live
113|  holds are not invalidated, so the running task finishes and reports
114|  normally, then the runner takes no further work from the unloaded project.
115|- Runner workdir hygiene supports churn: per-assignment reap plus a
116|  ~1-minute terminal-workdir sweep; `WORKTREE_CAP=5` evicts LRU *stale*
117|  workdirs and parks residue on `kb-recovery/*` branches, never deletes.
118|
119|Hitch H-3: `DELETE /projects/:id` is memory-only and unfenced — it removes
120|just the in-memory map entry (no config-file/registry removal, so a rescan
121|resurrects it) and does not invalidate that project's live claims. A task
122|in-flight across a delete keeps its lease until TTL expiry and its progress
123|calls still resolve (task files remain on disk). For runner fleet use this
124|is contained (leases expire, work re-queues), but deletion mid-flight is
125|not a clean unload. Follow-up: fence holds + remove persisted state, or
126|document "scope-off first, delete only when idle".
127|
128|### Q4 — Runners take tasks from multiple projects — PASS WITH HITCH
129|
130|One runner interleaves across projects sequentially (one assignment at a
131|time per daemon; each poll may serve a different project); the fleet
132|parallelises. Attribution and fencing verified by code + a live probe:
133|
134|- Every runner call carries the task's own `projectId` plus
135|  `executionId`/`epoch` (`claim`, `claimHeartbeat`, `progress`, `logs`,
136|  `verifySha`, `steerAck`, `integration*`).
137|- Task ids are `uuidv4` (globally unique,
138|  [taskLifecycle.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/api/work/taskLifecycle.js) ~L259);
139|  claims are keyed by task id globally with monotonic backend epochs
140|  (never wall-clock — immune to host clock skew).
141|- Task lookup is project-scoped: `taskStore.getTask(projectId, taskId)` —

98|### Q3 — Projects loaded/unloaded from runners — PASS WITH HITCH
99|
100|Load/unload *from runners* works with drain-and-fence semantics and no
101|restart on the operator path:
102|
103|- Load: `POST /projects/register` → idempotent `registerProjectPath`
104|  (re-register is a no-op) + `ProjectStore` rescan; registry file is
105|  advisory (missing/corrupt → empty, never broken boot).
106|- Runner-side scope: `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_PROJECTS` allowlist, sent on every
107|  `dispatchClaim` poll; empty = serve all.
108|- Operator-side unload at runtime: `PATCH /runners/:id/config`
109|  `{ projectScope: [...] }` (persisted, no restart), enforced on dispatch,
110|  direct claim, and merge-lease paths by the single point
111|  `operatorConfigVerdict` → loud `PROJECT_SCOPE` refusal, never silent skip.
112|- In-flight work drains: scope changes touch only future matching — live
113|  holds are not invalidated, so the running task finishes and reports
114|  normally, then the runner takes no further work from the unloaded project.
115|- Runner workdir hygiene supports churn: per-assignment reap plus a
116|  ~1-minute terminal-workdir sweep; `WORKTREE_CAP=5` evicts LRU *stale*
117|  workdirs and parks residue on `kb-recovery/*` branches, never deletes.
118|
119|Hitch H-3: `DELETE /projects/:id` is memory-only and unfenced — it removes
120|just the in-memory map entry (no config-file/registry removal, so a rescan
121|resurrects it) and does not invalidate that project's live claims. A task
122|in-flight across a delete keeps its lease until TTL expiry and its progress
123|calls still resolve (task files remain on disk). For runner fleet use this
124|is contained (leases expire, work re-queues), but deletion mid-flight is
125|not a clean unload. Follow-up: fence holds + remove persisted state, or
126|document "scope-off first, delete only when idle".

129|
130|One runner interleaves across projects sequentially (one assignment at a
131|time per daemon; each poll may serve a different project); the fleet
132|parallelises. Attribution and fencing verified by code + a live probe:
133|
134|- Every runner call carries the task's own `projectId` plus
135|  `executionId`/`epoch` (`claim`, `claimHeartbeat`, `progress`, `logs`,
136|  `verifySha`, `steerAck`, `integration*`).
137|- Task ids are `uuidv4` (globally unique,
138|  [taskLifecycle.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/api/work/taskLifecycle.js) ~L259);

140|  (never wall-clock — immune to host clock skew).

98|### Q3 — Projects loaded/unloaded from runners — PASS WITH HITCH
99|
100|Load/unload *from runners* works with drain-and-fence semantics and no
101|restart on the operator path:
102|
103|- Load: `POST /projects/register` → idempotent `registerProjectPath`
104|  (re-register is a no-op) + `ProjectStore` rescan; registry file is
105|  advisory (missing/corrupt → empty, never broken boot).
106|- Runner-side scope: `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_PROJECTS` allowlist, sent on every
107|  `dispatchClaim` poll; empty = serve all.
108|- Operator-side unload at runtime: `PATCH /runners/:id/config`
109|  `{ projectScope: [...] }` (persisted, no restart), enforced on dispatch,
110|  direct claim, and merge-lease paths by the single point
111|  `operatorConfigVerdict` → loud `PROJECT_SCOPE` refusal, never silent skip.
112|- In-flight work drains: scope changes touch only future matching — live
113|  holds are not invalidated, so the running task finishes and reports
114|  normally, then the runner takes no further work from the unloaded project.
115|- Runner workdir hygiene supports churn: per-assignment reap plus a
116|  ~1-minute terminal-workdir sweep; `WORKTREE_CAP=5` evicts LRU *stale*
117|  workdirs and parks residue on `kb-recovery/*` branches, never deletes.
118|
119|Hitch H-3: `DELETE /projects/:id` is memory-only and unfenced — it removes
120|just the in-memory map entry (no config-file/registry removal, so a rescan
121|resurrects it) and does not invalidate that project's live claims. A task
122|in-flight across a delete keeps its lease until TTL expiry and its progress
123|calls still resolve (task files remain on disk). For runner fleet use this
124|is contained (leases expire, work re-queues), but deletion mid-flight is
125|not a clean unload. Follow-up: fence holds + remove persisted state, or
126|document "scope-off first, delete only when idle".
127|
128|### Q4 — Runners take tasks from multiple projects — PASS WITH HITCH
129|
130|One runner interleaves across projects sequentially (one assignment at a
131|time per daemon; each poll may serve a different project); the fleet
132|parallelises. Attribution and fencing verified by code + a live probe:
133|
134|- Every runner call carries the task's own `projectId` plus
135|  `executionId`/`epoch` (`claim`, `claimHeartbeat`, `progress`, `logs`,
136|  `verifySha`, `steerAck`, `integration*`).
137|- Task ids are `uuidv4` (globally unique,
138|  [taskLifecycle.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/api/work/taskLifecycle.js) ~L259);
139|  claims are keyed by task id globally with monotonic backend epochs
140|  (never wall-clock — immune to host clock skew).
141|- Task lookup is project-scoped: `taskStore.getTask(projectId, taskId)` —
142|  a wrong-project replay finds no task and the route 404s before any write.
143|- Probe `/tmp/kb-q4-probe.mjs` (temp state only, cleaned after) observed:
144|  correct-project progress accepted; cross-project lookup → null (route
145|  404); stale epoch → `STALE_EPOCH`; second claimer → `CLAIM_CONFLICT`.
146|- Workdir/branch isolation: per-task worktree `kb-<taskId>` on branch
147|  `kb/<taskId>` (uuid-keyed, collision-free across projects).
148|
149|Hitch H-4 (defense in depth): the execution ledger never compares
150|`hold.projectId` to the request's projectId — `ClaimStore.describe()`
151|strips `projectId` from its projection, so `_holdOrThrow` cannot check it.
152|Cross-project safety therefore rests on uuid uniqueness + scoped lookup +
153|unguessable lease tokens (all sound), but a belt-and-braces projectId
154|comparison is missing. The probe confirmed a *crafted colliding id* would
155|be accepted. Fix: include `projectId` in `describe()` and compare in the
156|ledger guard. Not a blocker (uuidv4 collision is infeasible and lease
157|tokens are unguessable), but cheap to close.

1|# AUDIT.md — Multi-project production-readiness audit
2|
3|Task: `5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085` — review the multi-project
4|mechanisms to confirm KainBain can handle production-level workloads across
5|multiple projects at once (untested since runners were implemented).
6|
7|Guidance: [FRAMEWORKS.md](./FRAMEWORKS.md) (ISO 25010 spine, 29119 tests, SRE
8|bar, Twelve-Factor runner lifecycle, named queue patterns, ASVS V4/V5).
9|Survey inputs: [INTENT-SURVEY.md](./INTENT-SURVEY.md),
10|[FEEDBACK_SURVEY.md](./FEEDBACK_SURVEY.md).
11|
12|## 0. Survey responses — disposition
13|
14|Both survey files were read. Their `answers` blocks are empty (no operator
15|selections recorded), so per the survey's own "Auditor's choice / judgement
16|call" options this audit proceeds on auditor's judgement with these
17|recorded interpretations (each maps to one FEEDBACK_SURVEY question):
18|
19|| Survey Q | Interpretation used |
20||---|---|
21|| q1 queue model | Pass = one shared central queue drained in central-queue order, OR per-project queues with a shared pool + documented fairness — whichever exists must show no silos, no unbounded starvation, no silent drops. (Found: the former.) |
22|| q2 load/unload | Pass = drain-and-fence semantics: in-flight work finishes or is safely parked, no new claims after unload, re-load resumes cleanly. Hard-detach or restart-required unload would be a hitch/blocker. |
23|| q3 switch + interleave | All four guarantees required: switch never interrupts others; one runner interleaves with correct projectId; cross-project writes rejected; git/workdir isolation holds. |
24|| q4 skills | All four behaviours required: merge-not-replace; per-project-only shadowing; project-agnostic core skills; invalid/oversized never crashes a stage. |

28|
29|## 1. Verdict
30|
31|**READY WITH HITCHES for small-scale multi-project use (2–3 concurrent
32|projects, 1–2 runners) — the "start developing apps" goal. NOT YET PROVEN at
33|production scale: the SRE SLO gate (FRAMEWORKS §6) is open.**
34|
35|- Zero blockers found in Q1–Q7. Every must-have mechanism exists, is wired,
36|  and is covered by passing tests re-run in this audit (187 tests green).
37|- Five hitches (H-1…H-5) and three observations (O-1…O-3) are recorded below
38|  with owners' next actions. None stops app-development use.
39|- Q8 is `not yet measurable` per SRE Ch.3 (no declared SLOs, no load/soak or
40|  failure drills executed here). §7 proposes the SLO set and the drill list
41|  that closes the gate. Do not claim production-scale readiness until that
42|  gate is run.
43|
44|## 2. Per-check results
45|
46|### Q1 — Switch projects without interrupting others — PASS
47|
48|Switching is a view-layer id flip with no execution coupling:
49|
50|- Backend: `POST /projects/:id/activate` → `projectStore.setActiveProject`
51|  ([projects.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/api/routes/projects.js) ~L612).
52|  It only sets `activeProjectId`; no task, claim, scheduler, or runner state
53|  is touched.
54|- Dispatch (`scanClaimableTasks`,
55|  [scanClaimableTasks.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/api/flow/dispatch/scanClaimableTasks.js))
56|  and the embedded scheduler
57|  ([findNextCandidateTask.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/api/flow/scheduler/findNextCandidateTask.js))
58|  iterate `projectStore.listProjects()` — all projects, never the active one.
59|- The runner daemon never reads the active project; every call carries an
60|  explicit `projectId` ([client.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/runner/client.js)).
61|- The multi-runner monitor resolves each hold from the held task's own
62|  project, "never from whatever pipeline the viewer has selected"
63|  ([runnerRoutes.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/api/flow/runnerRoutes.js) ~L523).
64|- Worktree bulkhead: per-workdir promise chains (`workdirChains`,
65|  [project.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/runner/project.js))
66|  serialize git per workdir, and stale-lock recovery refuses to act while a
67|  live git process runs — one wedged project cannot stall another's git.
68|
69|Hitch H-1 (see §3): runner-mutating endpoints resolve a *missing* projectId
70|to the active project instead of rejecting (fail-open default tenant).
71|
72|### Q2 — Multiple projects collapse to one queue — PASS
73|
74|One shared central queue, not per-project silos:
75|
76|- `scanClaimableTasks` scans every project (allowlist-filtered only by the
77|  runner's own `projectIds`) and sorts through the single shared seam
78|  `sortCentralQueue`, used identically by runner dispatch, the embedded
79|  scheduler, and the queue display — the three can never disagree about
80|  "what runs next".
81|- Order: oldest-waiting-first globally, furthest-along percentage tiebreak,
82|  15-minute starvation ceiling (overdue jumps ahead oldest-first)
83|  ([centralQueuePolicy.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/api/flow/scheduler/centralQueuePolicy.js)).
84|- Contention safety: the claim fence (`ClaimStore.claim`, `CLAIM_CONFLICT`
85|  on lost races) is the single arbiter; concurrent loops poll again rather
86|  than double-dispatch. `noDoubleDispatch.test.js` passes.
87|- Backpressure: fleet-wide cap → HTTP 429 `FLEET_CONCURRENCY_EXHAUSTED`
88|  (daemon backs off *without* consuming idle budget); per-project cap skips
89|  that project's candidates (`PROJECT_BUSY`) instead of blocking the queue.
90|- Tests re-run green: `scanClaimableTasks.test.js` (6),
91|  `centralQueueFairness.test.js` (7), `runnerDispatchCaps.test.js`,
92|  `runnerPolicyDispatch.test.js`, `noDoubleDispatch.test.js`.
93|
94|Hitch H-2: fairness is FIFO-only with no per-project quota — a sustained
95|burst from one project delays others up to the ceiling. Documented tradeoff,
96|not a correctness failure.
97|
98|### Q3 — Projects loaded/unloaded from runners — PASS WITH HITCH
99|
100|Load/unload *from runners* works with drain-and-fence semantics and no
101|restart on the operator path:
102|
103|- Load: `POST /projects/register` → idempotent `registerProjectPath`
104|  (re-register is a no-op) + `ProjectStore` rescan; registry file is
105|  advisory (missing/corrupt → empty, never broken boot).
106|- Runner-side scope: `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_PROJECTS` allowlist, sent on every
107|  `dispatchClaim` poll; empty = serve all.
108|- Operator-side unload at runtime: `PATCH /runners/:id/config`
109|  `{ projectScope: [...] }` (persisted, no restart), enforced on dispatch,
110|  direct claim, and merge-lease paths by the single point
111|  `operatorConfigVerdict` → loud `PROJECT_SCOPE` refusal, never silent skip.
112|- In-flight work drains: scope changes touch only future matching — live
113|  holds are not invalidated, so the running task finishes and reports
114|  normally, then the runner takes no further work from the unloaded project.
115|- Runner workdir hygiene supports churn: per-assignment reap plus a
116|  ~1-minute terminal-workdir sweep; `WORKTREE_CAP=5` evicts LRU *stale*
117|  workdirs and parks residue on `kb-recovery/*` branches, never deletes.
118|
119|Hitch H-3: `DELETE /projects/:id` is memory-only and unfenced — it removes
120|just the in-memory map entry (no config-file/registry removal, so a rescan
121|resurrects it) and does not invalidate that project's live claims. A task
122|in-flight across a delete keeps its lease until TTL expiry and its progress
123|calls still resolve (task files remain on disk). For runner fleet use this
124|is contained (leases expire, work re-queues), but deletion mid-flight is
125|not a clean unload. Follow-up: fence holds + remove persisted state, or
126|document "scope-off first, delete only when idle".
127|
128|### Q4 — Runners take tasks from multiple projects — PASS WITH HITCH
129|
130|One runner interleaves across projects sequentially (one assignment at a
131|time per daemon; each poll may serve a different project); the fleet
132|parallelises. Attribution and fencing verified by code + a live probe:
133|
134|- Every runner call carries the task's own `projectId` plus
135|  `executionId`/`epoch` (`claim`, `claimHeartbeat`, `progress`, `logs`,
136|  `verifySha`, `steerAck`, `integration*`).
137|- Task ids are `uuidv4` (globally unique,
138|  [taskLifecycle.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/api/work/taskLifecycle.js) ~L259);
139|  claims are keyed by task id globally with monotonic backend epochs
140|  (never wall-clock — immune to host clock skew).
141|- Task lookup is project-scoped: `taskStore.getTask(projectId, taskId)` —
142|  a wrong-project replay finds no task and the route 404s before any write.
143|- Probe `/tmp/kb-q4-probe.mjs` (temp state only, cleaned after) observed:
144|  correct-project progress accepted; cross-project lookup → null (route
145|  404); stale epoch → `STALE_EPOCH`; second claimer → `CLAIM_CONFLICT`.
146|- Workdir/branch isolation: per-task worktree `kb-<taskId>` on branch
147|  `kb/<taskId>` (uuid-keyed, collision-free across projects).
148|
149|Hitch H-4 (defense in depth): the execution ledger never compares
150|`hold.projectId` to the request's projectId — `ClaimStore.describe()`
151|strips `projectId` from its projection, so `_holdOrThrow` cannot check it.
152|Cross-project safety therefore rests on uuid uniqueness + scoped lookup +
153|unguessable lease tokens (all sound), but a belt-and-braces projectId
154|comparison is missing. The probe confirmed a *crafted colliding id* would
155|be accepted. Fix: include `projectId` in `describe()` and compare in the
156|ledger guard. Not a blocker (uuidv4 collision is infeasible and lease
157|tokens are unguessable), but cheap to close.
158|
159|### Q5 — No hard-coded / assumed `kainbain` core project — PASS
160|
161|Three-pass hunt (text + structural + runtime reasoning). Zero true
162|assumptions found. Full disposition table in §4; summary:
163|
164|- Dispatch, claim, scheduler, skills, and registry paths never reference a
165|  `kainbain` project id/slug. Project identity is always carried explicitly
166|  or enumerated from the store/registry.
167|- "First project" defaults are order-based, never name-based
168|  (`scanProjects` first-key active default; UI `data[0]` fallback with
169|  stored-id preference). No path requires a project *named* kainbain, first,
170|  or active to function.
171|- Runtime-rename reasoning: the suites re-run here (`scanClaimableTasks`,
172|  `centralQueueFairness`, `skillsRegistry`, `claimStore`,
173|  `runnerPolicyDispatch`, `integrationDispatch`, …) all execute against
174|  synthetic non-`kainbain` slugs in temp roots and pass — equivalent in
175|  coverage to the FRAMEWORKS rename test for the audited paths.
176|
177|### Q6 — Per-project custom skills + shared core skills — PASS
178|
179|The overlay model meets all four required behaviours:
180|
181|- Merge, not replace: `mergeSkillSources({ globalSkills, projectSkills })`
182|  retains both rows; the UI shows "Shadows default" for overrides.
183|- Per-project-only shadowing: `loadSkill` / `SkillsRegistry.getSkill` prefer
184|  `<projectCwd>/skills/<name>` for that project only; project B's
185|  resolution is untouched by project A's overlay. A same-dir guard
186|  (`isDistinctOverlay`) handles the self-managed KainBain case where the
187|  project dir *is* the global library dir.
188|- Project-agnostic core skills: the prompt engine binds lookup to the
189|  task's own `projectCwd`
190|  ([promptCuration.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/api/promptCuration.js) ~L219-225),
191|  and per-stage `skills[i].config` overrides resolve per attachment —
192|  same core skill, different keywords per project/stage, no bleed.
193|- Invalid/oversized never crashes a stage: invalid frontmatter/config →
194|  `invalid: true` descriptor, never throws; oversized bodies rejected as
195|  invalid without being read whole; injection caps total chars
196|  (`maxChars`, default 16000) with visible
197|  `[skill <name> omitted: size cap]` markers; unknown skills land in
198|  `omitted`, not exceptions.
199|- Tests re-run green: `skillsRegistry.test.js` (55), `skillInjection.test.js`
200|  (all), plus prompt-curation keyword/contract suites in the wider run.
201|
202|### Q7 — Test without creating real projects — PASS
203|
204|The synthetic strategy is fully supported and was used by this audit:
205|
206|- Backstop verified present and correct: `api/testSetup.isolation.js`
207|  (vitest `setupFiles` — temp projects/notes/circuit/registry roots before
208|  any import) plus the per-file `api/isolatedTestRoots.js` convention
209|  (temp projects, notes, registry, claim/runner/steer/fleet state files,
210|  auth dir). `testIsolation.guard.test.js` passes.
211|- Seams used: constructor/env injection everywhere the audit touched
212|  (`ClaimStore({ stateFile })`, `KAINBAIN_*` env, `createRunnerClient({
213|  fetchImpl })`); no live root was written.
214|- Contamination check: `git status --short` clean after the audit;
215|  `api/node_modules` (installed to run tests) is git-ignored; the Q4 probe
216|  minted and deleted its own tmp dir (verified absent after); no writes to
217|  `~/projects`, `~/.kainbain/projects.json`, or `~/.kainbain/engine/*`
218|  were made. Zero real or dummy projects created, mutated, or deleted.
219|- Existing dummy projects were treated as read-only and were not needed.
220|
221|### Q8 — Production-level workloads — NOT YET MEASURABLE (gate open)
222|
223|Per SRE Ch.3, no SLOs are declared anywhere in the repo, so no
224|"production ready at scale" verdict can be issued. What exists:
225|
226|- Backpressure primitives: fleet 429, per-project skip, circuit breaker
227|  (`Engine is tripped — dispatch is stopped`), claim TTL + lazy expiry +
228|  `STALE_EPOCH` fencing, idempotent completion (retried executionId is a
229|  no-op), worktree cap with recovery parking.
230|- Partial observability: `queueDepth` + scheduler stats + git contention in
231|  [observabilityMetrics.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/api/watch/observabilityMetrics.js);
232|  `staleRejected` ledger counters; `/runners/monitor` live holds. Missing:
233|  dispatch-latency percentiles, per-project throughput/fairness counters,
234|  claim success rate — H-5.
235|- Quarantine exists only for models, not for poison tasks; poison-task,
236|  runner-kill, and backend-restart drills were not executed in this stage.
237|
238|§7 proposes the SLO set and drill list that close this gate. The Q1–Q7

72|### Q2 — Multiple projects collapse to one queue — PASS
73|
74|One shared central queue, not per-project silos:
75|
76|- `scanClaimableTasks` scans every project (allowlist-filtered only by the
77|  runner's own `projectIds`) and sorts through the single shared seam
78|  `sortCentralQueue`, used identically by runner dispatch, the embedded
79|  scheduler, and the queue display — the three can never disagree about
80|  "what runs next".
81|- Order: oldest-waiting-first globally, furthest-along percentage tiebreak,
82|  15-minute starvation ceiling (overdue jumps ahead oldest-first)

85|  on lost races) is the single arbiter; concurrent loops poll again rather
86|  than double-dispatch. `noDoubleDispatch.test.js` passes.
87|- Backpressure: fleet-wide cap → HTTP 429 `FLEET_CONCURRENCY_EXHAUSTED`
88|  (daemon backs off *without* consuming idle budget); per-project cap skips
89|  that project's candidates (`PROJECT_BUSY`) instead of blocking the queue.

98|### Q3 — Projects loaded/unloaded from runners — PASS WITH HITCH
99|
100|Load/unload *from runners* works with drain-and-fence semantics and no
101|restart on the operator path:
102|
103|- Load: `POST /projects/register` → idempotent `registerProjectPath`
104|  (re-register is a no-op) + `ProjectStore` rescan; registry file is
105|  advisory (missing/corrupt → empty, never broken boot).
106|- Runner-side scope: `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_PROJECTS` allowlist, sent on every
107|  `dispatchClaim` poll; empty = serve all.
108|- Operator-side unload at runtime: `PATCH /runners/:id/config`
109|  `{ projectScope: [...] }` (persisted, no restart), enforced on dispatch,
110|  direct claim, and merge-lease paths by the single point
111|  `operatorConfigVerdict` → loud `PROJECT_SCOPE` refusal, never silent skip.
112|- In-flight work drains: scope changes touch only future matching — live
113|  holds are not invalidated, so the running task finishes and reports
114|  normally, then the runner takes no further work from the unloaded project.
115|- Runner workdir hygiene supports churn: per-assignment reap plus a
116|  ~1-minute terminal-workdir sweep; `WORKTREE_CAP=5` evicts LRU *stale*
117|  workdirs and parks residue on `kb-recovery/*` branches, never deletes.
118|
119|Hitch H-3: `DELETE /projects/:id` is memory-only and unfenced — it removes
120|just the in-memory map entry (no config-file/registry removal, so a rescan
121|resurrects it) and does not invalidate that project's live claims. A task
122|in-flight across a delete keeps its lease until TTL expiry and its progress
123|calls still resolve (task files remain on disk). For runner fleet use this
124|is contained (leases expire, work re-queues), but deletion mid-flight is
125|not a clean unload. Follow-up: fence holds + remove persisted state, or
126|document "scope-off first, delete only when idle".
127|
128|### Q4 — Runners take tasks from multiple projects — PASS WITH HITCH
129|
130|One runner interleaves across projects sequentially (one assignment at a
131|time per daemon; each poll may serve a different project); the fleet
132|parallelises. Attribution and fencing verified by code + a live probe:
133|
134|- Every runner call carries the task's own `projectId` plus
135|  `executionId`/`epoch` (`claim`, `claimHeartbeat`, `progress`, `logs`,
136|  `verifySha`, `steerAck`, `integration*`).
137|- Task ids are `uuidv4` (globally unique,
138|  [taskLifecycle.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/api/work/taskLifecycle.js) ~L259);
139|  claims are keyed by task id globally with monotonic backend epochs
140|  (never wall-clock — immune to host clock skew).
141|- Task lookup is project-scoped: `taskStore.getTask(projectId, taskId)` —
142|  a wrong-project replay finds no task and the route 404s before any write.
143|- Probe `/tmp/kb-q4-probe.mjs` (temp state only, cleaned after) observed:
144|  correct-project progress accepted; cross-project lookup → null (route
145|  404); stale epoch → `STALE_EPOCH`; second claimer → `CLAIM_CONFLICT`.
146|- Workdir/branch isolation: per-task worktree `kb-<taskId>` on branch
147|  `kb/<taskId>` (uuid-keyed, collision-free across projects).
148|
149|Hitch H-4 (defense in depth): the execution ledger never compares
150|`hold.projectId` to the request's projectId — `ClaimStore.describe()`
151|strips `projectId` from its projection, so `_holdOrThrow` cannot check it.
152|Cross-project safety therefore rests on uuid uniqueness + scoped lookup +
153|unguessable lease tokens (all sound), but a belt-and-braces projectId
154|comparison is missing. The probe confirmed a *crafted colliding id* would
155|be accepted. Fix: include `projectId` in `describe()` and compare in the
156|ledger guard. Not a blocker (uuidv4 collision is infeasible and lease
157|tokens are unguessable), but cheap to close.

1|# AUDIT.md — Multi-project production-readiness audit
2|
3|Task: `5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085` — review the multi-project
4|mechanisms to confirm KainBain can handle production-level workloads across
5|multiple projects at once (untested since runners were implemented).
6|
7|Guidance: [FRAMEWORKS.md](./FRAMEWORKS.md) (ISO 25010 spine, 29119 tests, SRE
8|bar, Twelve-Factor runner lifecycle, named queue patterns, ASVS V4/V5).
9|Survey inputs: [INTENT-SURVEY.md](./INTENT-SURVEY.md),
10|[FEEDBACK_SURVEY.md](./FEEDBACK_SURVEY.md).
11|
12|## 0. Survey responses — disposition
13|
14|Both survey files were read. Their `answers` blocks are empty (no operator
15|selections recorded), so per the survey's own "Auditor's choice / judgement
16|call" options this audit proceeds on auditor's judgement with these
17|recorded interpretations (each maps to one FEEDBACK_SURVEY question):
18|
19|| Survey Q | Interpretation used |
20||---|---|
21|| q1 queue model | Pass = one shared central queue drained in central-queue order, OR per-project queues with a shared pool + documented fairness — whichever exists must show no silos, no unbounded starvation, no silent drops. (Found: the former.) |
22|| q2 load/unload | Pass = drain-and-fence semantics: in-flight work finishes or is safely parked, no new claims after unload, re-load resumes cleanly. Hard-detach or restart-required unload would be a hitch/blocker. |
23|| q3 switch + interleave | All four guarantees required: switch never interrupts others; one runner interleaves with correct projectId; cross-project writes rejected; git/workdir isolation holds. |
24|| q4 skills | All four behaviours required: merge-not-replace; per-project-only shadowing; project-agnostic core skills; invalid/oversized never crashes a stage. |
25|| q5 hard-coding | True `kainbain`-as-project assumptions = blocker. Benign strings (product name, sample data, fallbacks) = observation with disposition. |
26|| q6 synthetic testing | Ephemeral temp-dir fixtures with auto-cleanup + contamination checks (live dummy projects read-only, never mutated, none added). |
27|| q7/q8 scale bar | Auditor's judgement: no full load rig in this stage; small-scale bar (2–3 projects, 1–2 runners) judged on code + unit/integration evidence, full production-scale SLO gate left explicitly open with a proposed SLO set. |
28|
29|## 1. Verdict
30|
31|**READY WITH HITCHES for small-scale multi-project use (2–3 concurrent
32|projects, 1–2 runners) — the "start developing apps" goal. NOT YET PROVEN at
33|production scale: the SRE SLO gate (FRAMEWORKS §6) is open.**
34|
35|- Zero blockers found in Q1–Q7. Every must-have mechanism exists, is wired,
36|  and is covered by passing tests re-run in this audit (187 tests green).
37|- Five hitches (H-1…H-5) and three observations (O-1…O-3) are recorded below
38|  with owners' next actions. None stops app-development use.
39|- Q8 is `not yet measurable` per SRE Ch.3 (no declared SLOs, no load/soak or
40|  failure drills executed here). §7 proposes the SLO set and the drill list
41|  that closes the gate. Do not claim production-scale readiness until that
42|  gate is run.
43|
44|## 2. Per-check results
45|
46|### Q1 — Switch projects without interrupting others — PASS
47|
48|Switching is a view-layer id flip with no execution coupling:
49|
50|- Backend: `POST /projects/:id/activate` → `projectStore.setActiveProject`
51|  ([projects.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/api/routes/projects.js) ~L612).
52|  It only sets `activeProjectId`; no task, claim, scheduler, or runner state
53|  is touched.
54|- Dispatch (`scanClaimableTasks`,
55|  [scanClaimableTasks.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/api/flow/dispatch/scanClaimableTasks.js))
56|  and the embedded scheduler
57|  ([findNextCandidateTask.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/api/flow/scheduler/findNextCandidateTask.js))
58|  iterate `projectStore.listProjects()` — all projects, never the active one.
59|- The runner daemon never reads the active project; every call carries an
60|  explicit `projectId` ([client.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/runner/client.js)).
61|- The multi-runner monitor resolves each hold from the held task's own
62|  project, "never from whatever pipeline the viewer has selected"
63|  ([runnerRoutes.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/api/flow/runnerRoutes.js) ~L523).
64|- Worktree bulkhead: per-workdir promise chains (`workdirChains`,
65|  [project.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/runner/project.js))
66|  serialize git per workdir, and stale-lock recovery refuses to act while a
67|  live git process runs — one wedged project cannot stall another's git.
68|
69|Hitch H-1 (see §3): runner-mutating endpoints resolve a *missing* projectId
70|to the active project instead of rejecting (fail-open default tenant).
71|
72|### Q2 — Multiple projects collapse to one queue — PASS
73|
74|One shared central queue, not per-project silos:
75|
76|- `scanClaimableTasks` scans every project (allowlist-filtered only by the
77|  runner's own `projectIds`) and sorts through the single shared seam
78|  `sortCentralQueue`, used identically by runner dispatch, the embedded
79|  scheduler, and the queue display — the three can never disagree about
80|  "what runs next".
81|- Order: oldest-waiting-first globally, furthest-along percentage tiebreak,
82|  15-minute starvation ceiling (overdue jumps ahead oldest-first)
83|  ([centralQueuePolicy.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/api/flow/scheduler/centralQueuePolicy.js)).
84|- Contention safety: the claim fence (`ClaimStore.claim`, `CLAIM_CONFLICT`
85|  on lost races) is the single arbiter; concurrent loops poll again rather
86|  than double-dispatch. `noDoubleDispatch.test.js` passes.
87|- Backpressure: fleet-wide cap → HTTP 429 `FLEET_CONCURRENCY_EXHAUSTED`
88|  (daemon backs off *without* consuming idle budget); per-project cap skips
89|  that project's candidates (`PROJECT_BUSY`) instead of blocking the queue.
90|- Tests re-run green: `scanClaimableTasks.test.js` (6),
91|  `centralQueueFairness.test.js` (7), `runnerDispatchCaps.test.js`,
92|  `runnerPolicyDispatch.test.js`, `noDoubleDispatch.test.js`.
93|
94|Hitch H-2: fairness is FIFO-only with no per-project quota — a sustained
95|burst from one project delays others up to the ceiling. Documented tradeoff,
96|not a correctness failure.
97|
98|### Q3 — Projects loaded/unloaded from runners — PASS WITH HITCH
99|
100|Load/unload *from runners* works with drain-and-fence semantics and no
101|restart on the operator path:
102|
103|- Load: `POST /projects/register` → idempotent `registerProjectPath`
104|  (re-register is a no-op) + `ProjectStore` rescan; registry file is
105|  advisory (missing/corrupt → empty, never broken boot).
106|- Runner-side scope: `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_PROJECTS` allowlist, sent on every
107|  `dispatchClaim` poll; empty = serve all.
108|- Operator-side unload at runtime: `PATCH /runners/:id/config`
109|  `{ projectScope: [...] }` (persisted, no restart), enforced on dispatch,
110|  direct claim, and merge-lease paths by the single point
111|  `operatorConfigVerdict` → loud `PROJECT_SCOPE` refusal, never silent skip.
112|- In-flight work drains: scope changes touch only future matching — live
113|  holds are not invalidated, so the running task finishes and reports
114|  normally, then the runner takes no further work from the unloaded project.
115|- Runner workdir hygiene supports churn: per-assignment reap plus a
116|  ~1-minute terminal-workdir sweep; `WORKTREE_CAP=5` evicts LRU *stale*
117|  workdirs and parks residue on `kb-recovery/*` branches, never deletes.
118|
119|Hitch H-3: `DELETE /projects/:id` is memory-only and unfenced — it removes
120|just the in-memory map entry (no config-file/registry removal, so a rescan
121|resurrects it) and does not invalidate that project's live claims. A task
122|in-flight across a delete keeps its lease until TTL expiry and its progress
123|calls still resolve (task files remain on disk). For runner fleet use this
124|is contained (leases expire, work re-queues), but deletion mid-flight is
125|not a clean unload. Follow-up: fence holds + remove persisted state, or
126|document "scope-off first, delete only when idle".
127|
128|### Q4 — Runners take tasks from multiple projects — PASS WITH HITCH
129|
130|One runner interleaves across projects sequentially (one assignment at a
131|time per daemon; each poll may serve a different project); the fleet
132|parallelises. Attribution and fencing verified by code + a live probe:
133|
134|- Every runner call carries the task's own `projectId` plus
135|  `executionId`/`epoch` (`claim`, `claimHeartbeat`, `progress`, `logs`,
136|  `verifySha`, `steerAck`, `integration*`).
137|- Task ids are `uuidv4` (globally unique,
138|  [taskLifecycle.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/api/work/taskLifecycle.js) ~L259);
139|  claims are keyed by task id globally with monotonic backend epochs
140|  (never wall-clock — immune to host clock skew).
141|- Task lookup is project-scoped: `taskStore.getTask(projectId, taskId)` —
142|  a wrong-project replay finds no task and the route 404s before any write.
143|- Probe `/tmp/kb-q4-probe.mjs` (temp state only, cleaned after) observed:
144|  correct-project progress accepted; cross-project lookup → null (route
145|  404); stale epoch → `STALE_EPOCH`; second claimer → `CLAIM_CONFLICT`.
146|- Workdir/branch isolation: per-task worktree `kb-<taskId>` on branch
147|  `kb/<taskId>` (uuid-keyed, collision-free across projects).
148|
149|Hitch H-4 (defense in depth): the execution ledger never compares
150|`hold.projectId` to the request's projectId — `ClaimStore.describe()`
151|strips `projectId` from its projection, so `_holdOrThrow` cannot check it.
152|Cross-project safety therefore rests on uuid uniqueness + scoped lookup +
153|unguessable lease tokens (all sound), but a belt-and-braces projectId
154|comparison is missing. The probe confirmed a *crafted colliding id* would
155|be accepted. Fix: include `projectId` in `describe()` and compare in the
156|ledger guard. Not a blocker (uuidv4 collision is infeasible and lease
157|tokens are unguessable), but cheap to close.
158|
159|### Q5 — No hard-coded / assumed `kainbain` core project — PASS
160|
161|Three-pass hunt (text + structural + runtime reasoning). Zero true
162|assumptions found. Full disposition table in §4; summary:
163|
164|- Dispatch, claim, scheduler, skills, and registry paths never reference a
165|  `kainbain` project id/slug. Project identity is always carried explicitly
166|  or enumerated from the store/registry.

169|  stored-id preference). No path requires a project *named* kainbain, first,
170|  or active to function.
171|- Runtime-rename reasoning: the suites re-run here (`scanClaimableTasks`,
172|  `centralQueueFairness`, `skillsRegistry`, `claimStore`,
173|  `runnerPolicyDispatch`, `integrationDispatch`, …) all execute against
174|  synthetic non-`kainbain` slugs in temp roots and pass — equivalent in

178|
179|The overlay model meets all four required behaviours:

200|  (all), plus prompt-curation keyword/contract suites in the wider run.
201|
202|### Q7 — Test without creating real projects — PASS
203|
204|The synthetic strategy is fully supported and was used by this audit:
205|
206|- Backstop verified present and correct: `api/testSetup.isolation.js`
207|  (vitest `setupFiles` — temp projects/notes/circuit/registry roots before

223|Per SRE Ch.3, no SLOs are declared anywhere in the repo, so no

332|   writes, or reports (error-budget-zero item).

tool.result:
Read text file `docs/tasks/5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/AUDIT.md`.
1|# AUDIT.md — Multi-project production-readiness audit
2|
3|Task: `5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085` — review the multi-project
4|mechanisms to confirm KainBain can handle production-level workloads across
5|multiple projects at once (untested since runners were implemented).
6|
7|Guidance: [FRAMEWORKS.md](./FRAMEWORKS.md) (ISO 25010 spine, 29119 tests, SRE
8|bar, Twelve-Factor runner lifecycle, named queue patterns, ASVS V4/V5).
9|Survey inputs: [INTENT-SURVEY.md](./INTENT-SURVEY.md),
10|[FEEDBACK_SURVEY.md](./FEEDBACK_SURVEY.md).
11|
12|## 0. Survey responses — disposition
13|
14|Both survey files were read. Their `answers` blocks are empty (no operator
15|selections recorded), so per the survey's own "Auditor's choice / judgement
16|call" options this audit proceeds on auditor's judgement with these
17|recorded interpretations (each maps to one FEEDBACK_SURVEY question):
18|
19|| Survey Q | Interpretation used |
20||---|---|
21|| q1 queue model | Pass = one shared central queue drained in central-queue order, OR per-project queues with a shared pool + documented fairness — whichever exists must show no silos, no unbounded starvation, no silent drops. (Found: the former.) |
22|| q2 load/unload | Pass = drain-and-fence semantics: in-flight work finishes or is safely parked, no new claims after unload, re-load resumes cleanly. Hard-detach or restart-required unload would be a hitch/blocker. |
23|| q3 switch + interleave | All four guarantees required: switch never interrupts others; one runner interleaves with correct projectId; cross-project writes rejected; git/workdir isolation holds. |
24|| q4 skills | All four behaviours required: merge-not-replace; per-project-only shadowing; project-agnostic core skills; invalid/oversized never crashes a stage. |
25|| q5 hard-coding | True `kainbain`-as-project assumptions = blocker. Benign strings (product name, sample data, fallbacks) = observation with disposition. |
26|| q6 synthetic testing | Ephemeral temp-dir fixtures with auto-cleanup + contamination checks (live dummy projects read-only, never mutated, none added). |
27|| q7/q8 scale bar | Auditor's judgement: no full load rig in this stage; small-scale bar (2–3 projects, 1–2 runners) judged on code + unit/integration evidence, full production-scale SLO gate left explicitly open with a proposed SLO set. |
28|
29|## 1. Verdict
30|
31|**READY WITH HITCHES for small-scale multi-project use (2–3 concurrent
32|projects, 1–2 runners) — the "start developing apps" goal. NOT YET PROVEN at
33|production scale: the SRE SLO gate (FRAMEWORKS §6) is open.**
34|
35|- Zero blockers found in Q1–Q7. Every must-have mechanism exists, is wired,
36|  and is covered by passing tests re-run in this audit (187 tests green).
37|- Five hitches (H-1…H-5) and three observations (O-1…O-3) are recorded below
38|  with owners' next actions. None stops app-development use.
39|- Q8 is `not yet measurable` per SRE Ch.3 (no declared SLOs, no load/soak or
40|  failure drills executed here). §7 proposes the SLO set and the drill list
41|  that closes the gate. Do not claim production-scale readiness until that
42|  gate is run.
43|
44|## 2. Per-check results
45|
46|### Q1 — Switch projects without interrupting others — PASS
47|
48|Switching is a view-layer id flip with no execution coupling:
49|
50|- Backend: `POST /projects/:id/activate` → `projectStore.setActiveProject`
51|  ([projects.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/api/routes/projects.js) ~L612).
52|  It only sets `activeProjectId`; no task, claim, scheduler, or runner state
53|  is touched.
54|- Dispatch (`scanClaimableTasks`,
55|  [scanClaimableTasks.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/api/flow/dispatch/scanClaimableTasks.js))
56|  and the embedded scheduler
57|  ([findNextCandidateTask.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/api/flow/scheduler/findNextCandidateTask.js))
58|  iterate `projectStore.listProjects()` — all projects, never the active one.
59|- The runner daemon never reads the active project; every call carries an
60|  explicit `projectId` ([client.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/runner/client.js)).
61|- The multi-runner monitor resolves each hold from the held task's own
62|  project, "never from whatever pipeline the viewer has selected"
63|  ([runnerRoutes.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/api/flow/runnerRoutes.js) ~L523).
64|- Worktree bulkhead: per-workdir promise chains (`workdirChains`,
65|  [project.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/runner/project.js))
66|  serialize git per workdir, and stale-lock recovery refuses to act while a
67|  live git process runs — one wedged project cannot stall another's git.
68|
69|Hitch H-1 (see §3): runner-mutating endpoints resolve a *missing* projectId
70|to the active project instead of rejecting (fail-open default tenant).
71|
72|### Q2 — Multiple projects collapse to one queue — PASS
73|
74|One shared central queue, not per-project silos:
75|
76|- `scanClaimableTasks` scans every project (allowlist-filtered only by the
77|  runner's own `projectIds`) and sorts through the single shared seam
78|  `sortCentralQueue`, used identically by runner dispatch, the embedded
79|  scheduler, and the queue display — the three can never disagree about
80|  "what runs next".
81|- Order: oldest-waiting-first globally, furthest-along percentage tiebreak,
82|  15-minute starvation ceiling (overdue jumps ahead oldest-first)
83|  ([centralQueuePolicy.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/api/flow/scheduler/centralQueuePolicy.js)).
84|- Contention safety: the claim fence (`ClaimStore.claim`, `CLAIM_CONFLICT`
85|  on lost races) is the single arbiter; concurrent loops poll again rather
86|  than double-dispatch. `noDoubleDispatch.test.js` passes.
87|- Backpressure: fleet-wide cap → HTTP 429 `FLEET_CONCURRENCY_EXHAUSTED`
88|  (daemon backs off *without* consuming idle budget); per-project cap skips
89|  that project's candidates (`PROJECT_BUSY`) instead of blocking the queue.
90|- Tests re-run green: `scanClaimableTasks.test.js` (6),
91|  `centralQueueFairness.test.js` (7), `runnerDispatchCaps.test.js`,
92|  `runnerPolicyDispatch.test.js`, `noDoubleDispatch.test.js`.
93|
94|Hitch H-2: fairness is FIFO-only with no per-project quota — a sustained
95|burst from one project delays others up to the ceiling. Documented tradeoff,
96|not a correctness failure.
97|
98|### Q3 — Projects loaded/unloaded from runners — PASS WITH HITCH
99|
100|Load/unload *from runners* works with drain-and-fence semantics and no
101|restart on the operator path:
102|
103|- Load: `POST /projects/register` → idempotent `registerProjectPath`
104|  (re-register is a no-op) + `ProjectStore` rescan; registry file is
105|  advisory (missing/corrupt → empty, never broken boot).
106|- Runner-side scope: `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_PROJECTS` allowlist, sent on every
107|  `dispatchClaim` poll; empty = serve all.
108|- Operator-side unload at runtime: `PATCH /runners/:id/config`
109|  `{ projectScope: [...] }` (persisted, no restart), enforced on dispatch,
110|  direct claim, and merge-lease paths by the single point
111|  `operatorConfigVerdict` → loud `PROJECT_SCOPE` refusal, never silent skip.
112|- In-flight work drains: scope changes touch only future matching — live
113|  holds are not invalidated, so the running task finishes and reports
114|  normally, then the runner takes no further work from the unloaded project.
115|- Runner workdir hygiene supports churn: per-assignment reap plus a
116|  ~1-minute terminal-workdir sweep; `WORKTREE_CAP=5` evicts LRU *stale*
117|  workdirs and parks residue on `kb-recovery/*` branches, never deletes.
118|
119|Hitch H-3: `DELETE /projects/:id` is memory-only and unfenced — it removes
120|just the in-memory map entry (no config-file/registry removal, so a rescan
121|resurrects it) and does not invalidate that project's live claims. A task
122|in-flight across a delete keeps its lease until TTL expiry and its progress
123|calls still resolve (task files remain on disk). For runner fleet use this
124|is contained (leases expire, work re-queues), but deletion mid-flight is
125|not a clean unload. Follow-up: fence holds + remove persisted state, or
126|document "scope-off first, delete only when idle".
127|
128|### Q4 — Runners take tasks from multiple projects — PASS WITH HITCH
129|
130|One runner interleaves across projects sequentially (one assignment at a
131|time per daemon; each poll may serve a different project); the fleet
132|parallelises. Attribution and fencing verified by code + a live probe:
133|
134|- Every runner call carries the task's own `projectId` plus
135|  `executionId`/`epoch` (`claim`, `claimHeartbeat`, `progress`, `logs`,
136|  `verifySha`, `steerAck`, `integration*`).
137|- Task ids are `uuidv4` (globally unique,
138|  [taskLifecycle.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/api/work/taskLifecycle.js) ~L259);
139|  claims are keyed by task id globally with monotonic backend epochs
140|  (never wall-clock — immune to host clock skew).
141|- Task lookup is project-scoped: `taskStore.getTask(projectId, taskId)` —
142|  a wrong-project replay finds no task and the route 404s before any write.
143|- Probe `/tmp/kb-q4-probe.mjs` (temp state only, cleaned after) observed:
144|  correct-project progress accepted; cross-project lookup → null (route
145|  404); stale epoch → `STALE_EPOCH`; second claimer → `CLAIM_CONFLICT`.
146|- Workdir/branch isolation: per-task worktree `kb-<taskId>` on branch
147|  `kb/<taskId>` (uuid-keyed, collision-free across projects).
148|
149|Hitch H-4 (defense in depth): the execution ledger never compares
150|`hold.projectId` to the request's projectId — `ClaimStore.describe()`
151|strips `projectId` from its projection, so `_holdOrThrow` cannot check it.
152|Cross-project safety therefore rests on uuid uniqueness + scoped lookup +
153|unguessable lease tokens (all sound), but a belt-and-braces projectId
154|comparison is missing. The probe confirmed a *crafted colliding id* would
155|be accepted. Fix: include `projectId` in `describe()` and compare in the
156|ledger guard. Not a blocker (uuidv4 collision is infeasible and lease
157|tokens are unguessable), but cheap to close.
158|
159|### Q5 — No hard-coded / assumed `kainbain` core project — PASS
160|
161|Three-pass hunt (text + structural + runtime reasoning). Zero true
162|assumptions found. Full disposition table in §4; summary:
163|
164|- Dispatch, claim, scheduler, skills, and registry paths never reference a
165|  `kainbain` project id/slug. Project identity is always carried explicitly
166|  or enumerated from the store/registry.
167|- "First project" defaults are order-based, never name-based
168|  (`scanProjects` first-key active default; UI `data[0]` fallback with
169|  stored-id preference). No path requires a project *named* kainbain, first,
170|  or active to function.
171|- Runtime-rename reasoning: the suites re-run here (`scanClaimableTasks`,
172|  `centralQueueFairness`, `skillsRegistry`, `claimStore`,
173|  `runnerPolicyDispatch`, `integrationDispatch`, …) all execute against
174|  synthetic non-`kainbain` slugs in temp roots and pass — equivalent in
175|  coverage to the FRAMEWORKS rename test for the audited paths.
176|
177|### Q6 — Per-project custom skills + shared core skills — PASS
178|
179|The overlay model meets all four required behaviours:
180|
181|- Merge, not replace: `mergeSkillSources({ globalSkills, projectSkills })`
182|  retains both rows; the UI shows "Shadows default" for overrides.
183|- Per-project-only shadowing: `loadSkill` / `SkillsRegistry.getSkill` prefer
184|  `<projectCwd>/skills/<name>` for that project only; project B's
185|  resolution is untouched by project A's overlay. A same-dir guard
186|  (`isDistinctOverlay`) handles the self-managed KainBain case where the
187|  project dir *is* the global library dir.
188|- Project-agnostic core skills: the prompt engine binds lookup to the
189|  task's own `projectCwd`

1|# FRAMEWORKS.md — Auditor guidance for the multi-project / runner production-readiness audit
2|
3|Task: `5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085` — "Review the multi project mechanisms to ensure that we are good to handle production level workloads. Able to switch projects without interrupting others; multiple projects collapse to one queue for runners; projects loaded/unloaded from runners; runners take tasks from multiple projects; no hard-coded/assumed `kainbain` core project; per-project custom skills plus shared core skills; test multi-project behaviour without creating real projects."
4|
5|This document does **not** perform the audit. It tells the auditor which industry-standard frameworks to use, how to apply each to KainBain, what evidence to collect, and what counts as a blocker versus a hitch. Read it before opening the chosen framework documents.
6|
7|## 0. How to use this document
8|
9|- §1 decomposes the task into auditable questions. §2 is the framework map (one line each). §3 is the per-framework apply-guide. §4 is the per-check playbook the auditor executes. §5–§7 are method notes for the two hardest parts (synthetic projects; the hard-coding hunt). §8–§10 define severity, entry/exit criteria, and the evidence pack.
10|- Cite framework clauses in the audit report (e.g. `ISO/IEC 25010:2023 §5.2.2`, `SRE Ch.17`, `ASVS 4.0 V4.1.1`). A finding without a framework anchor is an opinion, not an audit result.
11|- All version pins below are **2026-11-15 current**. Verify the pin at audit start; if a newer edition exists, note the delta and audit to the newer edition.
12|- Working directory / evidence roots for the auditor: `runner/` (daemon, client, project workdirs), `api/projectStore.js`, `api/projectRegistry.js`, `api/projectResolution.js`, `api/skills/skillsRegistry.js`, `api/skills/skillInjection.js`, `api/isolatedTestRoots.js`, `shared/` (stages/skills conventions). The live roots `~/projects/*`, `~/.kainbain/projects.json`, `~/.kainbain/engine/*` are **evidence sources for read-only inspection only — never mutation targets** (see §5 guardrails).
13|
14|## 1. Task decomposition — auditable questions
15|
16|| # | Task clause | Audit question | Primary frameworks |
17||---|---|---|---|
18|| Q1 | Switch projects without interrupting others | Is project context (active project, sessions, tasks, runners, docs) isolated so switching one project never cancels, reassigns, or starves another? | ISO 25010 portability/compatibility; Twelve-Factor IX (disposability); SRE Ch.7 (capacity/toil); Bulkhead pattern |
19|| Q2 | Multiple projects collapse to one queue for runners | Does `dispatchClaim({ projectIds })` (`runner/client.js`, `runner/daemon.js`, `runner/config.js` `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_PROJECTS`) serve a single mixed queue without per-project silos, head-of-line blocking, or starvation? | Competing-consumers / priority-queue patterns; SRE Ch.5 (load balancing); KEDA/HPA resource model; ISO 25010 performance efficiency |
20|| Q3 | Projects loaded/unloaded from runners | Can a project be registered/adopted and later removed such that runners stop claiming its tasks, in-flight work drains or is fenced, and re-load is clean? | Twelve-Factor III/X (config, disposability); ATAM lifecycle; compensating-transaction pattern |
21|| Q4 | Runners take tasks from multiple different projects | Can one runner instance (and a fleet) interleave tasks across projects correctly — correct `projectId` on claim/progress/verify/steer, no cross-project write? | Multi-tenancy isolation (OWASP ASVS V4); Competing-consumers; ISO 25010 functional suitability |
22|| Q5 | No hard-coded / assumed `kainbain` core project | Are there no defaults, fallbacks, seed/demo paths, docs, or UI strings that silently assume the `kainbain` project exists or is first/active? | ATAM coupling/cohesion; ISO 25010 maintainability (modularity, reusability); OWASP secure-coding (no default-tenant) |
23|| Q6 | Per-project custom skills + access to core skills | Does the global skill library + per-project `<projectRoot>/skills/` overlay (shadowing, `mergeSkillSources`/`loadSkill` in `skillsRegistry.js`, injection in `skillInjection.js`) give each project independent skills while core skills remain usable across projects with different stage configs? | Plugin/overlay pattern; ISO 25010 maintainability (reusability); ISO 29119 functional test design |
24|| Q7 | Test multi-project behaviour without creating real projects | Is there a safe synthetic/ephemeral fixture strategy (temp roots, fakes, mock harness) that exercises Q1–Q6 without polluting `~/projects/*` or the live registry? | ISO/IEC 29119 test design; xUnit test-doubles (Fowler); Testcontainers/ephemeral-environment practice; SRE test-in-prod |
25|| Q8 | Production-level workloads; blockers/hitches | Under realistic concurrent multi-project load, does the system meet explicit throughput/latency/availability objectives, and are capacity, fairness, and failure modes bounded? | Google SRE (SLOs, error budgets, capacity, golden signals); ISO 25010 performance efficiency + reliability; DORA throughput/stability |

27|## 2. Framework map — what to open and why
28|
29|| Framework (pinned edition) | Use it for | Skip it for |
30||---|---|---|
31|| **ISO/IEC 25010:2023** *Systems and software quality models* | The audit's top-level quality spine: functional suitability, performance efficiency, compatibility, reliability, security, maintainability, portability. Every finding maps to a characteristic + sub-characteristic. | Specific queueing maths or test-case syntax (delegated below). |
32|| **ISO/IEC 29119-1/-2/-3/-4/-5:2022-2025** *Software testing* | Test process, test design techniques (equivalence partitioning, state transition, combinatorial), test types (functional, integration, system, load/performance), and entry/exit criteria for Q7/Q8. | Product quality judgement (that is 25010). |
33|| **Google SRE Book (2017) + SRE Workbook (2018)**, Ch. 3, 5, 7, 17–19 | SLOs/error budgets, capacity & load balancing, handling overload, production-readiness checklist, postmortem/blameless review. The "production level" bar for Q8. | Application-level API design. |
34|| **Twelve-Factor App (12factor.net, rev. 2023)** | Runner as a worker process: config in env, disposability, concurrency, admin processes, dev/prod parity — Q1, Q3. | Queue semantics (use patterns below). |
35|| **Microsoft Azure Architecture Center — design patterns** (Bulkhead, Competing Consumers, Priority Queue, Idempotent Consumer, Circuit Breaker, Poison Pill / Dead-Letter, Compensating Transaction) + **Enterprise Integration Patterns** (Hohpe, 2003) | Vocabulary and acceptance logic for Q1–Q4 queue/failure behaviour. Cite the named pattern, not an ad-hoc description. | Language-specific implementation. |
36|| **OWASP ASVS 4.0 (V4/V5) + OWASP Top 10:2021** (esp. A01 Broken Access Control / BOLA) | Cross-project isolation is an authorisation problem: can project A read/write/claim project B's tasks, docs, or skills? Q4, Q5, Q6. | General app hardening (out of scope). |
37|| **CNCF / Kubernetes multi-tenancy & KEDA practice** (namespaces, quotas, fair scheduling; KEDA scaled-objects/queue-length autoscaling) | Resource isolation and "collapse to one queue" fairness: quotas, noisy-neighbour, scale on queue depth. Analogy framework — KainBain is not Kubernetes; borrow the concepts, not the tooling. | Any claim that KainBain must run on Kubernetes. |
38|| **OpenTelemetry (1.x) + RED/USE method + SRE golden signals** | Observability acceptance: what metrics/logs/traces must exist to prove Q1/Q2/Q8 in production. | UI dashboards (out of scope). |
39|| **ATAM (Architecture Tradeoff Analysis Method, SEI) + C4 model + Nygard ADRs** | Architecture evaluation for coupling (Q5) and load/unload lifecycle (Q3); record tradeoff decisions as ADRs. | Re-litigation of past ADRs (read them as evidence). |
40|| **ISTQB / ISO 25010 testability + Fowler test-doubles (mocks, fakes, stubs, in-memory fakes)** | Q7 synthetic-project strategy: how to build ephemeral projects without real repos. | Load-test tooling choice (k6/Locust is the auditor's pick, §6). |
41|| **NIST CSF 2.0 (2024) / ISO 27001:2022 A.8** (supporting, optional) | Only if the audit touches credential/project-registration handling (`runner/credentialFile.js`, `projectRegistry.js`). Do not expand into a full security audit. | Full security compliance (explicitly out of scope). |
42|
43|Explicit non-frameworks (do not audit against): WCAG 2.2 (no UI in scope), ISO 13485/62304 (not medical), GDPR (no personal data in scope), SOC 2 full attestation (use CSF/ASVS slices only).
