45|## 3. Framework apply-guide — how to use each one on KainBain
46|
47|### 3.1 ISO/IEC 25010:2023 — the quality spine
48|
49|Map every finding to exactly one characteristic and sub-characteristic; a finding with no mapping is not yet a finding.
50|
51|| Characteristic | Sub-characteristics to test here | KainBain evidence to inspect |
52||---|---|---|
53|| Functional suitability (correctness, appropriateness) | Q2–Q4 claim/dispatch correctness, Q6 skill shadowing correctness | `runner/client.js` (`claim`, `dispatchClaim`), `runner/daemon.js` assignment loop, `api/skills/skillsRegistry.js` (`loadSkill`, `mergeSkillSources`), `api/skills/skillInjection.js` |
54|| Performance efficiency (time behaviour, resource utilisation, capacity) | Q2 queue throughput, Q8 concurrent dispatch, worktree cap (`WORKTREE_CAP`) pressure | `runner/project.js` (`WORKTREE_CAP`, `WORKTREE_EVICT_STALE_MS`), `runner/config.js`, daemon heartbeat/dispatch timings |
55|| Compatibility (co-existence, interoperability) | Runner↔backend API version (`runner/version.json`, `apiVersion`), multi-project co-existence on one host | `runner/daemon.js` `resolveRunnerBuild`, `runner/updates/*`, `api/projectStore.js` multi-root scan |
56|| Reliability (maturity, availability, fault tolerance, recoverability) | Q1 non-interruption, Q3 drain/fence, claim fencing (`executionId`/`epoch`), stale-lock recovery | `runner/project.js` (`maybeRecoverWorkdirLock`, `liveGitProcessRunning`), `runner/client.js` (`claimHeartbeat`, `verifySha`, `steerAck`) |
57|| Security (confidentiality, integrity, non-repudiation, accountability, authenticity) | Cross-project task/doc/skill access (BOLA), `projectId` spoofing on runner calls | Route guards via `api/projectResolution.js`, runner credential flow, `api/routes/files.js` `isPathSafe` |
58|| Maintainability (modularity, reusability, analysability, testability) | Q5 hard-coded assumptions, Q7 testability of multi-project seams | Grep/AST hunt (§7), `api/isolatedTestRoots.js` seams, injected `fetchImpl`/`runGit` seams in runner tests |
59|| Portability (installability, replaceability) | Load/unload (Q3), runner install/update with multi-project config | `runner/main.js`, `startRunner.sh`, `runner/updates/*`, `api/projectRegistry.js` |
60|
61|Report format per finding: `25010:<characteristic>/<sub-characteristic>` + severity (§8) + evidence path + reproduction.
62|
63|### 3.2 ISO/IEC 29119 — test process and design for Q7/Q8
64|
65|- **29119-1 (concepts):** name the test levels/types used — component (single store/registry), integration (store+registry+runner client), system (multi-project dispatch), and load/performance (Q8). Do not label everything "E2E".
66|- **29119-2 (process):** follow planning → design → implementation → execution → closure. The audit's test plan must state entry criteria (e.g. isolated roots available, mock harness registered), exit criteria (e.g. per-check pass counts in §4), and suspension criteria (live-root pollutions detected → stop, §5).
67|- **29119-4 (test design techniques — mandatory picks):** equivalence partitioning on `projectIds` (empty / single / multi / duplicate / unknown id); state-transition testing on project lifecycle (unloaded → loading → active → draining → unloaded); decision-table / combinatorial testing on runner config × project set; boundary-value analysis on `WORKTREE_CAP` and queue depth. Record which technique each test case uses.
68|- **29119-3 (test documentation):** every synthetic test cites its technique, preconditions (temp roots seed), oracle (expected `projectId` on claim/progress), and cleanup (`afterAll` deletes temp roots — the `api/isolatedTestRoots.js` contract).
69|- **29119-5 (keyword-driven / data-driven):** recommended for the multi-project matrix (project sets as rows) so the same suite runs against 2-project, N-project, and mixed queues without code changes.
70|
71|### 3.3 Google SRE — the "production level" bar (Q8)
72|
73|- **Ch.3 (SLOs):** the audit must *propose* SLOs before judging production readiness — e.g. dispatch latency p95, claim success rate, cross-project correctness (must be 100%), availability of the runner fleet. No SLO → no "production ready" verdict; report "not yet measurable" instead.
74|- **Ch.5 (load balancing / capacity):** queue-depth as the load signal; verify the single queue does not head-of-line block (§4 Q2) and that per-project bursts are absorbed or shed with backpressure, not by dropping other projects' tasks.
75|- **Ch.7 (handling overload / toil):** measure operational toil per project (manual load/unload, manual lease/credential recovery, manual worktree reaping). Production-level fails if each additional project adds linear toil.
76|- **Ch.17 (production readiness):** use as the checklist for Q8 closure — capacity, deployment/safety, monitoring, on-call runbooks for "project unloaded mid-task" and "runner fleet half-dead".
77|- **Workbook (postmortems):** any pre-existing multi-project incident (e.g. the worktree-fleet outage referenced in `runner/project.js`) must be written up blamelessly and referenced by the audit — do not re-litigate, verify the fix holds.
78|
79|### 3.4 Twelve-Factor App — runner as a worker (Q1, Q3)
80|
81|- **III (config in the environment):** `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_PROJECTS` and backend root envs (`PROJECTS_ROOT`, `KAINBAIN_PROJECTS_REGISTRY_FILE`) are the *only* project-set inputs — verify no project set is baked into code, defaults, or an image layer.
82|- **IX (disposability):** a runner must be killable at any point (mid-claim, mid-progress, mid-push) and the system must recover via fencing (`executionId`/`epoch`), lease expiry, and `kb-recovery/*` parking — never via manual cleanup assuming one project.
83|- **X (dev/prod parity):** synthetic Q7 fixtures must run the same dispatch/claim code path as production (mock harness allowed; mock queue not allowed).
84|- **V (build/release/run):** `runner/updates/*` + `version.json` build identity must not bake a project list into the bundle; audit the update manifest for project-scoped state.
85|
86|### 3.5 Named queue/failure patterns (Azure / Enterprise Integration Patterns) — Q1–Q4
87|
88|Cite the pattern per behaviour; a behaviour matching no named pattern is a design gap to report.
89|
90|| Pattern | Expected KainBain behaviour | Fails if |
91||---|---|---|
92|| **Competing Consumers** | N runners (or 1 runner, 2+ projects) drain one queue; each task claimed exactly once (fenced by `executionId`/`epoch`). | Two runners claim the same task; or a project is pinned to a runner. |
93|| **Priority Queue / fairness** | Burst from project A does not starve project B indefinitely; oldest-claimable wins or a documented fairness rule applies. | A single hot project blocks others past the SLO window (§4 Q2). |
94|| **Bulkhead** | Worktree/disk/git-lock bulkheads per workdir (`workdirChains` in `runner/project.js`) contain a wedged project. | One project's git lock or disk exhaustion stalls all projects. |
95|| **Idempotent Consumer** | Retried `claimHeartbeat`/`verifySha`/`steerAck`/`integrationReport` are safe to replay; epoch fencing rejects stale writers. | Replay double-applies progress, merges, or steers. |
96|| **Poison Pill + Dead-Letter** | A task that always fails (bad repo, bad skill, bad stage config) is quarantined after N attempts and does not wedge the queue for other projects. | One poison task blocks the mixed queue. |
97|| **Compensating Transaction** | Unload (Q3) parks unpushed work (`kb-recovery/*`), fences in-flight claims, and is reversible by re-load. | Unload deletes work or leaves a half-claimed task. |
98|| **Circuit Breaker** (for backends/harnesses) | A dead harness/model for one project does not consume all runner slots. | One broken harness starves the fleet. |
99|
100|### 3.6 OWASP ASVS 4.0 / Top 10:2021 — cross-project authorisation (Q4/Q5/Q6)
101|
102|- Treat every `projectId` on every runner-facing endpoint (`/tasks/:id/claim`, `/runners/dispatch`, `/runners/integration/*`, `/tasks/:id/progress|verify-sha|steer-ack`) as **object-level authorisation** (ASVS V4.1, V5.1; Top 10 A01/BOLA). Test: project A's runner credential/assignment cannot claim, progress, or report on project B's task by supplying B's `projectId`/`taskId`.
103|- Audit `api/projectResolution.js` (`resolveProjectId` falls back to the *active* project): any runner or API route that resolves "no id → active project" is a default-tenant smell (Q5). Runner endpoints must require an explicit `projectId` — flag any that silently default.
104|- Audit skill/doc file reads (`api/routes/files.js` `isPathSafe`, `skillsRegistry.js` `skillPathForName`) for path traversal *across* projects (symlink/overlay escape), not just within one project.
105|- Scope limit: this is an authorisation-pattern audit, not a full ASVS certification. Do not report unrelated ASVS items as blockers.
106|
107|### 3.7 CNCF/Kubernetes multi-tenancy + KEDA — resource isolation analogy
108|
109|Borrow concepts, not tooling: namespaces ≈ projects; quotas ≈ per-project worktree/concurrency caps; fair scheduling ≈ queue fairness (Q2); scale-on-queue-depth (KEDA) ≈ "collapse to one queue, scale runners on depth". The audit question is always: *what is KainBain's quota/fairness/scale signal for a project, and is it enforced?* If none exists, that is a production-readiness gap (SRE Ch.5), not a Kubernetes gap.
110|
111|### 3.8 OpenTelemetry + RED/USE + golden signals — observability acceptance
112|
113|For each of Q1/Q2/Q8 the audit must name the metric/log/trace that *proves* the behaviour in production. Minimum set: dispatch latency + queue depth (RED: rate/errors/duration), claim fencing rejections, per-project task throughput/fairness counters, worktree eviction count, skill-injection size-cap omissions. No signal → behaviour is unverifiable → report as "unmeasured" (fails SRE Ch.10), not as "passes".
114|
115|### 3.9 ATAM + C4 + Nygard ADRs — architecture evaluation (Q3, Q5)
116|
117|- Draw (or require) a C4 container/context view of backend ↔ runner ↔ projects ↔ skills. Any arrow labelled "assumes kainbain" is a Q5 finding.
118|- Run ATAM-style tradeoff analysis on: single-queue vs per-project queues (Q2), load/unload semantics (Q3), skill shadowing (Q6). Record each tradeoff as an ADR (Nygard format: context/decision/consequences) if one does not already exist.
119|- Past ADRs on the runner seam (e.g. ADR 0009 referenced in `runner/client.js`) are evidence: verify the implementation still matches the recorded decision.
120|
121|### 3.10 Test-doubles + ephemeral environments — Q7 strategy inputs
122|
123|- Fowler's taxonomy: prefer **fakes** (in-memory `ProjectStore`/`ProjectRegistry` over temp dirs) and **stubs** (mock harness, stub `fetchImpl`) over **mocks** that assert call counts; assert *outcomes* (correct `projectId`, drained queue) not interactions.
124|- Existing seams to reuse (do not invent new ones): `api/isolatedTestRoots.js` (`tempProjectsRoot`, `tempNotesRoot`, `tempIsolatedRegistryFile`, `tempStateFiles`), constructor injection (`new ProjectStore({ projectsRoot, registryFile })`, `createRunnerClient({ fetchImpl })`, `resolveRunnerBuild({ runGit })`), `runner` harness mock (`api/agent/harnesses/mock/`), `api/project/seedDemo.js` for demo fixtures.
125|- Ephemeral principle (Testcontainers practice): every multi-project test mints its own roots and deletes them in `afterAll`; no test may read/write the live `~/projects`, `~/.kainbain/projects.json`, or `~/.kainbain/engine/*` (the `testSetup.isolation.js` backstop — verify it still fires, §5).
126|
127|## 4. Per-check audit playbook — what to run for each question
128|
129|Each check lists: **framework lens → method → evidence → pass / blocker thresholds**. Severity definitions are in §8; do not downgrade a blocker because "it works for kainbain".
130|
131|### Q1 — Switch projects without interrupting others
132|
133|- Lens: 25010 portability + reliability; Twelve-Factor IX; Bulkhead.
134|- Method (29119 state-transition): seed projects A and B (synthetic, §5); start a long task in A (mock harness, slow stage); switch active project to B; complete a task in B; then verify A's task continued (heartbeats advancing, no re-claim, no lease loss) and B's completion did not touch A's worktree/docs/session.
135|- Evidence: daemon + backend logs showing A heartbeat continuity across the switch; `runner/project.js` worktree listing before/after; `api/sessionStore.js` TTL/sweep state.
136|- Pass: zero A-task interruption attributable to the switch. Blocker: switch cancels/reassigns/kills A work, or A's queue position is lost.
137|
138|### Q2 — Multiple projects collapse to one queue
139|
140|- Lens: Competing Consumers + Priority Queue/fairness; SRE Ch.5; KEDA scale-on-depth; 25010 capacity.
141|- Method: one runner configured with `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_PROJECTS=pA,pB` (via `runner/config.js`); enqueue N tasks for A, M for B, including an A-burst; observe claim order and completion. Repeat with A idle, B idle, and one project unregistered mid-burst.
142|- Evidence: `dispatchClaim({ projectIds })` request/response logs (`runner/client.js`, `runner/daemon.js` dispatch loop), per-project completion counters, queue-depth metric over time.
143|- Pass: both projects drain; no unbounded starvation (define the window in the test plan, e.g. every claimable task claimed within X s under load); burst from A does not delay B past the SLO. Blocker: per-project silos (separate queues the runner cannot see), head-of-line blocking, or silent task drops.
144|- Hitch (non-blocker): fairness is FIFO-only with no quota — record as a capacity tradeoff (ATAM) with a follow-up, not a correctness failure.
145|
146|### Q3 — Load / unload projects from runners
147|
148|- Lens: Twelve-Factor III/IX; Compensating Transaction; ATAM lifecycle; 25010 installability/recoverability.
149|- Method (state-transition: unloaded → loading → active → draining → unloaded → re-loaded): register/adopt project C (registry file + `ProjectStore` rescan); start a task; unload C mid-task; verify: no new claims for C, in-flight task either completes or is fenced/parked (`kb-recovery/*`), worktree handled per `reapTaskWorkdirIfTerminal`; re-load C; verify it re-registers cleanly with no duplicate/orphan state. Check the advisory-failure contract: corrupt/missing `projects.json` degrades to "no registered entries", never a broken boot (`api/projectRegistry.js`).
150|- Evidence: registry file diffs, runner config diffs, worktree/orphan listings (`listOrphanWorkdirs`, `reapTerminalOrphanWorkdirs`), claim-rejection codes after unload.
151|- Pass: unload is safe (no lost work, no zombie claims), re-load is idempotent (`registerProjectPath` no-op on re-register). Blocker: unload deletes unpushed work, leaves half-claimed tasks, or requires a runner/backend restart to take effect.
152|
153|### Q4 — Runners take tasks from multiple projects
154|
155|- Lens: OWASP ASVS V4/V5 + A01/BOLA; Competing Consumers; 25010 functional suitability.
156|- Method: one runner, projects A+B; enqueue interleaved tasks; assert every `claim`/`progress`/`verifySha`/`steerAck`/`integrationReport` call carries the task's own `projectId` and `executionId`; then negative tests: replay A's assignment against B's task (wrong `projectId`, stale `epoch`) and expect rejection.
157|- Evidence: captured runner-client call log (stub `fetchImpl` asserting payloads, as in `runner/client.test.js`), backend rejection codes.
158|- Pass: 100% correct `projectId` attribution; cross-project replay rejected with fencing errors. Blocker: any cross-project write, claim, or report accepted.
159|
160|### Q5 — No hard-coded / assumed `kainbain` core project
161|
162|- Lens: ATAM coupling; 25010 modularity/reusability; OWASP default-tenant.
163|- Method: §7 hunt (grep + AST + runtime rename test). Runtime test is decisive: rename/copy the core project to a non-`kainbain` slug in synthetic roots and run Q1–Q4 — everything must pass. Any code path that only works when the core project is named `kainbain`, is first, or is active is a finding.
164|- Evidence: grep hit list with disposition per hit (true assumption vs benign string vs test fixture), rename-test results.
165|- Pass: zero true assumptions. Blocker: any default/fallback/seed/UI path that requires the `kainbain` project to exist (see §7 for known hotspots: active-project fallback in `api/projectResolution.js`, demo seeding, docs-path defaults).
166|
167|### Q6 — Per-project custom skills + shared core skills
168|
169|- Lens: overlay/shadowing pattern; 25010 reusability; 29119 equivalence partitioning (shadowed / unshadowed / missing / invalid skill).
170|- Method (29119 decision table): global skill `S` with no overlay → core body injected; overlay `S` in project A only → A sees overlay, B sees global; invalid overlay (bad frontmatter/`KB_config.json`) → listed `invalid: true`, never throws, stage still runs (`skillsRegistry.js` contract); oversized skill → size-cap omission marker (`skillInjection.js`); core skill attached to stages in *different* projects with different `stage.skills[].config` keywords → each project resolves its own keywords (no cross-project keyword bleed).
171|- Evidence: `mergeSkillSources`/`loadSkill` resolution traces per project, injected prompt sections per project/stage, UI "Shadows default" rows.
172|- Pass: independent overlays, core skills reusable across projects, shadowing is per-project (A's overlay never changes B's resolution). Blocker: overlay leaks across projects, invalid skill crashes a stage, or core skills only work for the core project.
173|
174|### Q7 — Test without creating real projects
175|
176|- Lens: 29119 process; Fowler test-doubles; Testcontainers ephemeral principle.
177|- Method: §5 in full. Count real-project writes during the audit (must be zero); every test must mint and delete its own temp roots.
178|- Evidence: test file list + `afterAll` cleanup proof + live-roots untouched check (mtime/content hash of `~/projects`, `~/.kainbain/projects.json` before/after the audit run).
179|- Pass: full Q1–Q6 matrix executable synthetically. Blocker: any check that *requires* a real project to validate (means the seam is untestable — 25010 testability failure).
180|
181|### Q8 — Production-level workloads
182|
183|- Lens: SRE SLOs/error budgets/capacity; 25010 performance efficiency + reliability; RED/USE.
184|- Method: §6. Declare SLOs first (SRE Ch.3); then run the load profile; then the failure drills (runner kill mid-task, backend restart mid-dispatch, poison task, full disk/worktree cap).
185|- Evidence: SLO definitions, load results vs SLO, golden-signal dashboards/metrics, drill outcomes.
186|- Pass: SLOs defined and met under the agreed profile + drills recover without cross-project damage. Blocker: no SLO, or SLO missed, or any drill causes cross-project loss.
187|
188|## 5. Synthetic / no-real-projects strategy (Q7) — guardrails
189|
190|The user constraint is absolute: **do not create real projects** (the fleet already carries many dummy projects). The auditor's job is to prove Q1–Q6 with synthetic fixtures only.
191|
192|1. **Reuse the existing isolation backstop — never bypass it.** Every test file imports `api/isolatedTestRoots.js` *first* (before any `api/config.js` transitive import), which sets `PROJECTS_ROOT`, `NOTES_SPACE_ROOT`, and `KAINBAIN_PROJECTS_REGISTRY_FILE` to per-file `mkdtemp` dirs and mints per-file engine-state temp files. Verify `api/testSetup.isolation.js` still fails any suite that touches the live roots. If the backstop is missing or silent, that is a blocker for Q7 (untestable seams).
193|2. **Constructor/env injection, not globals.** `new ProjectStore({ projectsRoot, projectsRoots, notesRoot, registryFile })`, `createRunnerClient({ backendUrl, fetchImpl })`, `resolveRunnerBuild({ runGit })`, and runner `config.js` env (`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_PROJECTS`) are the seams. Tests pass temp values explicitly; no test edits the live registry or `~/projects`.
194|3. **Fixture shapes (29119-4):** two to three minimal synthetic projects (`proj-alpha`, `proj-beta`, optionally `proj-gamma`) as temp dirs containing only `.kainbain/project.json` (+ optional `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` overlay) and a git repo (bare or worktree as the test needs). No real remotes; git ops point at local temp remotes.
195|4. **Doubles:** mock harness (`api/agent/harnesses/mock/`) for slow/fast/failing stages; stub `fetchImpl` recording method/path/body for claim/dispatch assertions; in-memory fakes for `ProjectRegistry` where the file layer is not under test. Never mock the queue itself for Q2 (Twelve-Factor X parity) — mock the harness, keep the real dispatch path.
196|5. **Cleanup contract:** every fixture is created in `beforeEach`/`beforeAll` from temp roots and deleted in `afterAll` (the `isolatedTestRoots.js` header contract). Each test file mints its own roots — tests never share a registry file.
197|6. **Contamination check (run before and after the audit):** hash/ls `~/projects`, `~/.kainbain/projects.json`, `~/.kainbain/engine/*`; assert unchanged. Any audit step that writes live roots is stopped and reported as a process failure, not worked around.
198|7. **What "dummy projects already loaded" means for the audit:** treat existing dummy projects as *read-only evidence* of discovery behaviour (e.g. `ProjectStore` multi-root scan, `projectStore.multiroot.test.js`), never as mutation targets. If a check needs a clean slate, build it in temp roots — do not delete or rename live dummies.
199|
200|## 6. Production workload & capacity method (Q8)
201|
202|1. **Declare SLOs first (SRE Ch.3).** Minimum set the auditor must propose and then measure: (a) cross-project correctness = 100% (no silent mis-attribution — this is an error-budget-zero item); (b) dispatch latency p95 under the agreed profile; (c) claim success rate; (d) runner-fleet availability. If the team cannot agree SLOs, the audit verdict is "not yet measurable" — do not issue "production ready".
203|2. **Load profile (29119 load/performance type):** concurrent projects × tasks-per-project × burstiness, with at least: steady state, single-project burst (noisy neighbour), all-project burst, and sustained queue depth. Tool of auditor's choice (k6 or Locust recommended); record tool + script version in the evidence pack.
204|3. **Queueing check:** apply Little's law (`L = λW`) as a sanity oracle: predicted queue depth from arrival rate × wait time must match observed depth within tolerance — divergence indicates dropped or duplicated claims.
205|4. **Capacity limits to verify:** `WORKTREE_CAP` eviction behaviour (LRU + stale guard + `kb-recovery/*` parking, never deletion), git-lock contention (`workdirChains`), claim epoch fencing under retries, skill-injection size caps under many-skills-per-stage. Each limit must degrade *per project* (Bulkhead), never globally.
206|5. **Failure drills (SRE Ch.17):** kill a runner mid-task; restart backend mid-dispatch; submit a poison task (always-failing stage/skill/repo); fill worktrees to cap; unload a project mid-task (ties to Q3). Pass = recovery without cross-project loss; any cross-project damage is a blocker.
207|6. **Observability gate (OTel + golden signals):** the §3.8 metric set must exist and be queryable for the load+drill window. Missing signals = unverifiable = fail the Q8 gate until instrumented.
208|
209|## 7. Hard-coded `kainbain` hunt — method for Q5
210|
211|Run all three passes; a hit in any pass needs a disposition (true assumption / benign / fixture).
212|
213|- **Pass 1 — text search:** `kainbain` / `KainBain` / `KAINBAIN` across `api/`, `runner/`, `shared/`, `frontend/src/` (case-insensitive), excluding tests, docs, and version stamps. Flag: default project names/ids, "first project" logic, fallback-to-active, demo/seed paths (`api/project/seedDemo.js`), docs/UI strings naming the core project as the user, env-var defaults that name a project.
214|- **Pass 2 — structural search:** `getActiveProject()` callers (fallback semantics in `api/projectResolution.js` and routes); any `projects[0]` / `find(... ) ?? projects[0]` selection; any slug/alias defaulting to `kainbain`; any skill path or `SKILL.md` resolution that assumes the core project's overlay dir.
215|- **Pass 3 — runtime rename test (decisive):** in synthetic temp roots, copy the core project under a non-`kainbain` slug, remove/rename any `kainbain` project, and re-run Q1–Q4 + Q6. Everything must pass. A failure here is a blocker regardless of Pass 1–2 silence.
216|- Known hotspots to check first: `api/projectResolution.js` (active-project fallback leaking into runner paths), `api/projectStore.js` scan/seed defaults, `api/docsPath.js` / `api/kainbainDir.js` (per-project state-dir naming — must be project-agnostic), `api/skills/*` (global library reads must not assume the core project's dir), `runner/config.js` defaults, frontend "current project" defaults.
217|
218|## 8. Severity, blocker thresholds, and entry/exit criteria
219|
220|| Severity | Definition (audit-specific) | Effect on verdict |
221||---|---|---|
222|| **Blocker** | Breaks a Q1–Q8 must-have: cross-project data loss/corruption, cross-project unauthorised access, interruption of another project, unload deleting work, single-queue starvation/drop, hard-coded `kainbain` assumption, untestable seam (Q7), SLO defined and missed. | Audit verdict = **NOT production-ready** until fixed and re-tested. |
223|| **Hitch** | Works, but with documented pain: FIFO-only fairness with no quota, missing observability for one behaviour, toil scaling per project, eviction needing manual cleanup. | Production-ready *with* recorded follow-ups + owners; does not block. |
224|| **Observation** | Improvement opportunity with no behavioural impact (docs, naming, minor metric gaps). | Non-blocking; list in report. |
225|
226|- **Entry criteria (before auditing):** isolated-roots backstop verified (§5); synthetic fixtures for ≥2 projects buildable; SLOs proposed (§6.1); audit contamination snapshot taken (§5.6).
227|- **Exit criteria (to declare production-ready):** every Q1–Q6 check passes synthetically; Q7 contamination check clean; Q8 SLOs met + drills recovered; §7 hunt has zero true assumptions; all blockers fixed and re-tested; evidence pack (§9) complete. A pass claim without any one of these is invalid.
228|
229|## 9. Evidence pack — what the auditor must deliver
230|
231|1. **Framework-anchored findings register:** one row per finding — `question (Q1–Q8) | framework + clause | severity | evidence (file:line / log / metric) | reproduction | status`.
232|2. **Per-check results (§4):** pass/blocker per question with the exact commands, fixture shapes, and oracles used (29119-3 documentation).
233|3. **Synthetic-test inventory (§5):** test files, temp-root cleanup proof, contamination before/after hashes, confirmation that zero real projects were created or mutated.
234|4. **Load + drill report (§6):** SLO definitions, load tool/script versions, results vs SLO (including Little's-law check), drill outcomes.
235|5. **Hard-coding hunt (§7):** hit list with per-hit disposition + rename-test results.
236|6. **Skills matrix (§4 Q6):** shadowed/unshadowed/missing/invalid/oversized cases per project with resolution traces.
237|7. **ADR/tradeoff log (§3.9):** queue-fairness, unload-semantics, and shadowing tradeoffs with decisions (or "no ADR exists — recommend creating one").
238|8. **Verdict statement:** production-ready / ready-with-hitches / NOT production-ready — derived strictly from §8 exit criteria, citing the clause that decides it.
239|
240|## 10. References (pinned 2026-11-15)
241|
242|- ISO/IEC 25010:2023, *Systems and software Quality Models* (supersedes 2011).
243|- ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119-1/-2/-3/-4 (2022), -5 (2025), *Software testing*.
244|- Beyer et al., *Site Reliability Engineering* (O'Reilly, 2017), Ch. 3, 5, 7, 10, 17–19; *SRE Workbook* (2018).
245|- Wenger et al., *The Twelve-Factor App* (12factor.net, rev. 2023).
246|- Microsoft Learn, *Azure Architecture Center — Design patterns* (Bulkhead, Competing Consumers, Priority Queue, Idempotent Consumer, Circuit Breaker, Poison Pill, Compensating Transaction), accessed 2026-11-15; Hohpe, *Enterprise Integration Patterns* (Addison-Wesley, 2003).
247|- OWASP *Application Security Verification Standard* 4.0 (V4 access control, V5 validation) and *Top 10:2021* (A01 Broken Access Control).
248|- CNCF *Kubernetes multi-tenancy* guidance; KEDA *ScaledObject / queue-length scaling* documentation.
249|- OpenTelemetry *Specification 1.x*; SRE *RED/USE method* and *four golden signals*.
250|- Bass, Clements & Kazman, *Software Architecture in Practice* (ATAM); Brown et al., *C4 Model*; Nygard, *Architecture Decision Records* (2011).
251|- Fowler, *Mocks Aren't Stubs* / test-doubles taxonomy (martinfowler.com); ISTQB *Syllabus v4.0* test design techniques.
252|- NIST CSF 2.0 (2024) / ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A.8 (supporting slices only — runner credentials, registry handling).
253|- DORA / *Accelerate* (2018) throughput–stability metrics (supporting, for Q8 reporting).
254|
255|## 11. Auditor's one-page summary
256|
257|Audit to **ISO 25010** as the spine, **29119** for every test, **SRE** for the production bar, **Twelve-Factor** for runner lifecycle, **named queue patterns** for Q1–Q4 behaviour, and **ASVS V4/V5** for cross-project authorisation. Prove Q1–Q6 with **synthetic temp-root fixtures** behind the `isolatedTestRoots` backstop (never real projects), hunt hard-coding with **grep + structural search + the decisive rename test**, and declare production readiness only against **pre-declared SLOs + failure drills + complete evidence**. Everything else is a hitch or an observation.

{"content":"# DELIVERABLES.md — Multi-project production-readiness work packages

Task: `5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085` — make KainBain safe to run
multiple projects on shared runners at production-level workloads.

Source of truth: [AUDIT.md](./AUDIT.md) (verdict: READY WITH HITCHES at
small scale, 2–3 projects / 1–2 runners; production-scale gate open).
Guidance: [FRAMEWORKS.md](./FRAMEWORKS.md). Surveys:
[INTENT-SURVEY.md](./INTENT-SURVEY.md), [FEEDBACK_SURVEY.md](./FEEDBACK_SURVEY.md).

## How to read this file

- Each work package (WP) is a **whole, ticketable step**: one owner, one
  acceptance gate, shippable on its own. Ticket-splitting hints are inside
  each WP ("Slice into tickets").
- Ordering follows **"make the change easy, then make the change"** (Beck
  XP): structural seams and safety rails first (WP1–WP2), behaviour fixes
  next (WP3–WP4), measurement and drills once the signals exist (WP5),
  conditional scale-out only on evidence (WP6), config/docs last (WP7).
- Every WP states its **required knowledge** (files + framework clauses)
  so a ticket implementer never has to re-derive the audit.
- Global constraint on ALL WPs (from the task + AUDIT §6): **no real
  projects**. All verification uses ephemeral temp-dir fixtures
  (`proj-alpha`/`proj-beta`-style) behind `api/testSetup.isolation.js` +
  `api/isolatedTestRoots.js`, with before/after contamination checks on
  `~/projects`, `~/.kainbain/projects.json`, `~/.kainbain/engine/*`.
  Live dummy projects are read-only evidence, never mutation targets.
- Path note: AUDIT.md cites evidence under `/home/[REDACTED]/...`; the live
  checkout root differs but relative paths (`api/...`, `runner/...`,
  `frontend/...`) are identical. Resolve relatively.

## Dependency map

```
WP1 (tenant-safety seam) ──┐
WP2 (observability seam) ───┼──▶ WP5 (SLO gate + failure drills)
WP3 (lifecycle semantics) ──┘         │
WP4 (poison-task policy) ────────────┘
WP6 (fairness quota, CONDITIONAL on WP5 evidence) — standalone, off critical path
WP7 (runbooks/ADRs/docs, config-only) — last, depends on WP1+WP3+WP4+WP5 outcomes
```

- WP5 is blocked on WP1 (correctness must be fenced before load proves
  anything), WP2 (no SLO verdict without the signals), WP3 (unload drill
  needs defined semantics), WP4 (poison drill needs the policy).
- WP6 must NOT start before WP5 has numbers; it is explicitly conditional.
- WP7 is pure config/docs; do it last so it documents what was actually built.

---

## WP1 — Close the cross-project tenant-safety gap (H-1 + H-4)

**Goal:** make cross-project writes structurally impossible on the runner
path, not merely unlikely. Covers AUDIT H-1 (fail-open active-project
fallback) and H-4 (ledger never compares `hold.projectId`).

**Required knowledge**

- Files: `api/projectResolution.js` (`resolveProjectId`, lines ~8–14 —
  the `?? activeProject` fallback); `api/flow/runnerRoutes.js` (`guardedTask`
  ~L510, claim path ~L980, plus `progress`/`logs`/`verify-sha`/
  `complete-execution`/`steer-ack`/`interrupt` and `integration*` routes);
  `api/flow/claimStore.js` (`describe()` ~L230–239 — strips `projectId`);
  `api/flow/executionLedger.js` (`_holdOrThrow` ~L91–103 — checks only
  executionId/epoch/runnerId); `runner/client.js` (all calls already send
  explicit `projectId` — the fix must not break the daemon).
- Frameworks: OWASP ASVS 4.0 V4.1/V5.1 object-level authorisation
  (every `projectId` is a BOLA boundary); ISO 25010 security/integrity.
- Survey anchor: FEEDBACK_SURVEY q5 — true `kainbain`-as-project/default-
  tenant assumptions are **blockers**.

**Deliverables**

1. Explicit-`projectId` enforcement on all runner-mutating routes:
   missing `projectId` → `400` (never active-project fallback). Non-mutating
   UI/view routes may keep the fallback; document the split.
2. `ClaimStore.describe()` includes `projectId`; `_holdOrThrow` (or its
   successor guard) compares request `projectId` against `hold.projectId`
   and rejects mismatches with a named fencing error.
3. Regression tests (synthetic only): omitted-`projectId` → 400 on every
   mutated route; cross-project replay (A's lease against B's task, stale
   epoch, second claimer → `CLAIM_CONFLICT`/`STALE_EPOCH`/404) — extend the
   AUDIT Q4 probe (`/tmp/kb-q4-probe.mjs` pattern) into a committed suite.
4. Brief migration note: any current caller omitting `projectId` (AUDIT says
   none in the daemon — verify) is updated.

**Acceptance**

- Full Q4 matrix green on synthetic fixtures: correct-project writes
  accepted; wrong-project/stale-epoch/double-claim always rejected; no
  fallback-to-active on any mutating route.
- Existing suites still green: `claimStore`, `executionLedger`,
  `runnerPolicyDispatch`, `integrationDispatch`, `projectResolution`.

**Blocks / unblocks:** blocks WP5 (load must run against fenced code).
No dependency on other WPs — do first.

**Slice into tickets:** (a) route-guard + 400 tests; (b) ledger `projectId`
plumbing + fencing tests; (c) caller audit + migration note. (a) and (b) can
parallelise; (c) follows (a).

**Effort signal:** small–medium. Centralised guards, no queue/semantics change.

---

## WP2 — Add the missing production signals (H-5)

**Goal:** make multi-project behaviour *measurable* so the SLO gate (WP5)
can pass or fail honestly. Covers AUDIT H-5. This is the "make the change
easy" seam for everything quantitative.

**Required knowledge**

- Files: `api/watch/observabilityMetrics.js` (existing: `queueDepth`,
  scheduler stats, git contention); ledger `staleRejected` counters;
  `/runners/monitor` live-hold source; dispatch path (`api/flow/dispatch/
  scanClaimableTasks.js`, `api/flow/scheduler/centralQueuePolicy.js`,
  `sortCentralQueue`); fleet cap `429 FLEET_CONCURRENCY_EXHAUSTED` and
  per-project `PROJECT_BUSY` skip paths (new counters hook here).
- Frameworks: SRE Ch.10 / OTel + RED/USE + golden signals (FRAMEWORKS §3.8);
  minimum set per §3.8: dispatch latency, queue depth, claim-fencing
  rejections, per-project throughput/fairness, worktree evictions,
  skill size-cap omissions.

**Deliverables**

1. New counters/histograms: dispatch-latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99),
   per-project claimed/completed throughput + wait-time (feeds fairness),
   claim success rate (non-conflict claims / attempts, excluding operator
   pauses and version refusals), scope/fencing rejection breakdown
   (`PROJECT_SCOPE`, `STALE_EPOCH`, `CLAIM_CONFLICT`).
2. Metrics are per-project labelled and queryable over a load window
   (whatever the existing exposition is — extend it, don't add a second
   system).
3. Unit/integration tests on synthetic fixtures: each new signal moves
   under a scripted scenario (burst → fairness counters diverge correctly;
   conflict → conflict counter increments).
4. One-page metric dictionary (name, labels, what proves what) — feeds WP7.

**Acceptance**

- Every §3.8 minimum signal exists and is observable during a scripted
  synthetic burst; AUDIT's "unmeasured" list for Q8 is empty.
- No live-project writes during verification (contamination check clean).

**Blocks / unblocks:** blocks WP5 (SLOs need these signals). Independent of
WP1/WP3 — can parallelise with WP1.

**Slice into tickets:** (a) latency + queue-depth percentiles; (b) claim/
fencing + scope counters; (c) per-project throughput/fairness + dictionary.
All three can parallelise behind the agreed metric exposition.

**Effort signal:** small–medium. Additive instrumentation, no behaviour change.

---

## WP3 — Define and fence project unload/delete (H-3)

**Goal:** turn unload/delete from "mostly works, with a zombie window"
into a documented, fenced lifecycle. Covers AUDIT H-3 (`DELETE
/projects/:id` is memory-only, unfenced; rescan resurrects; live holds
survive until TTL).

**Required knowledge**

- Files: `api/routes/projects.js` (`DELETE /projects/:id` ~L602);
  `api/projectStore.js` (`deleteProject` ~L2006, rescan logic, first-key
  active default ~L529–530); registry file handling (`api/projectRegistry.js`
  — advisory, missing/corrupt → empty); operator scope path
  (`PATCH /runners/:id/config` `{ projectScope }` via `operatorConfigVerdict`
  — the *already-correct* drain-and-fence reference implementation: future
  matching only, live holds drain); `runner/project.js` workdir hygiene
  (`WORKTREE_CAP`, LRU evict, `kb-recovery/*` parking).
- Frameworks: Twelve-Factor III/IX (config, disposability); Compensating
  Transaction (unload parks + fences + is reversible); ISO 25010
  reliability/recoverability.
- Survey anchor: FEEDBACK_SURVEY q2 — drain-and-fence is the required
  semantic (in-flight finishes or parks, no new claims, re-load clean).

**Deliverables**

1. Decide and implement ONE of: (a) fence holds + remove persisted state
   (registry/config entries) on delete, or (b) keep delete shallow but
   refuse it while holds are live (`409` with active-hold list) and
   document "scope-off → wait idle → delete". AUDIT recommends (a) or the
   documented (b); do not leave the current silent-zombie behaviour.
2. State-transition tests (synthetic): active → scope-off mid-task (no new
   claims, in-flight drains) → delete → rescan does NOT resurrect →
   re-register is clean and idempotent (`registerProjectPath` no-op).
3. Operator error codes for post-unload claims (loud refusal, never silent
   skip — same contract as `PROJECT_SCOPE`).

**Acceptance**

- Mid-task unload/delete drill: zero lost work, zero zombie claims past
  the defined fence, re-load resumes cleanly.
- Advisory-registry contract preserved: corrupt/missing registry still
  degrades to empty, never broken boot.

**Blocks / unblocks:** blocks WP5's unload-mid-task drill. Independent of
WP1/WP2 — can parallelise.

**Slice into tickets:** (a) decision + fence/delete implementation;
(b) state-transition suite; (c) operator error UX. (b) pins (a)'s contract.

**Effort signal:** medium. Lifecycle semantics touch store + registry + routes.

---

## WP4 — Decide the poison-task policy (O-3)

**Goal:** answer AUDIT's open question — what happens to a task that can
never succeed — before it wedges the shared queue in production. Covers
O-3 (quarantine exists for models only; task-level dead-letter unverified).

**Required knowledge**

- Files: stage-failure paths (task fail vs requeue-loop — trace from the
  runner daemon through completion routes); existing model quarantine
  (reuse its shape if suitable); `WORKTREE_CAP` + `kb-recovery/*` parking
  (poison tasks also consume workdirs); WP2 counters (poison retries must
  be visible).
- Frameworks: Poison Pill + Dead-Letter pattern (FRAMEWORKS §3.5); SRE
  Ch.7 overload handling; ISO 25010 fault tolerance.
- Note: AUDIT Q2 backpressure (fleet 429, per-project skip, circuit
  breaker) already bounds *load*; this WP bounds *permanent failure*.

**Deliverables**

1. Policy decision recorded as ADR: retry budget (N attempts) → quarantine/
   dead-letter with reason preserved → queue continues for other projects;
   operator unquarantine path. (If current fail-fast already bounds it,
   the ADR records the proof + test instead of new code.)
2. Implementation if the proof fails: attempt counter, quarantine state,
   per-project quarantine visibility, no requeue-loop.
3. Synthetic tests: always-failing stage/skill/repo task → quarantined
   after N, sibling-project tasks drain unaffected.

**Acceptance**

- One poison task cannot stall the mixed queue; quarantine is observable
  (WP2 signals) and reversible by the operator.
- ADR filed (feeds WP7's tradeoff log).

**Blocks / unblocks:** blocks WP5's poison drill. Independent of WP1–WP3 —
can parallelise once the ADR direction is set.

**Slice into tickets:** (a) failure-path trace + ADR; (b) implementation
(if needed) + tests. (b) is conditional on (a)'s finding.

**Effort signal:** small if fail-fast already bounds it; medium if a
dead-letter store is built. Timebox the trace before committing to a build.

---

## WP5 — Run the production-scale gate: SLOs + load + failure drills (Q8)

**Goal:** close the AUDIT Q8 gate — either prove production-scale
readiness against pre-declared SLOs or produce the bounded failure list.
This WP makes no product change; it renders the verdict WP1–WP4 earned.
Do NOT claim production readiness without it.

**Required knowledge**

- AUDIT §7 proposal (adopt or amend first): correctness 100% (zero
  mis-attributed claims/progress/reports — error-budget-zero); dispatch
  latency p95 < 2 s under the agreed profile (after WP2); claim success
  rate > 99% (excl. operator pauses/version refusals); dispatch-endpoint
  non-5xx > 99.9% over the soak.
- Load profile (synthetic, mock harnesses, REAL dispatch path — never mock
  the queue, Twelve-Factor X parity): steady state (2–3 projects × few
  tasks) → single-project burst (noisy neighbour) → all-project burst →
  sustained queue depth; Little's-law sanity (`L = λW`) on depth.
- Failure drills: runner kill mid-task (lease expiry → re-queue, no
  cross-project loss); backend restart mid-dispatch (holds drop, epochs
  persist, re-queue as interrupted); poison task (WP4 policy); worktree-cap
  pressure (LRU + recovery parking); scope-off unload mid-task (WP3).
- Frameworks: SRE Ch.3/5/17 (SLOs, capacity, readiness checklist); 29119
  load/performance type; Bulkhead/Idempotent-Consumer/Circuit-Breaker
  expectations.

**Deliverables**

1. Agreed SLO set (signed off before the rig runs — SRE Ch.3 rule).
2. Load + drill report: tool + script versions, results vs each SLO,
   Little's-law check, per-drill outcome (recover clean / bounded damage /
   blocker found).
3. Verdict update: production-ready / ready-with-hitches / NOT ready, with
   the failing clause cited; any new blocker gets a WP1–WP4-style follow-up.

**Acceptance**

- SLOs declared BEFORE measurement; all drills executed on synthetic
  fixtures; contamination check clean; report filed in the task docs.
- Q8 exit criteria (FRAMEWORKS §8) all met, or the miss is named.

**Blocked by:** WP1 (fenced code), WP2 (signals), WP3 (unload semantics),
WP4 (poison policy). Starts only when all four land.

**Slice into tickets:** (a) SLO sign-off + rig + steady/burst runs;
(b) failure drills (one ticket per drill is fine — they parallelise);
(c) report + verdict. (a) first, (b) in any order, (c) last.

**Effort signal:** medium. Mostly rig + runs, not product code.

---

## WP6 — Fairness quota, ONLY on WP5 evidence (H-2, conditional)

**Goal:** decide with data whether FIFO-oldest-first + 15-minute ceiling
(`sortCentralQueue` in `api/flow/scheduler/centralQueuePolicy.js`) is
enough, or whether a noisy neighbour needs a per-project quota. Covers
AUDIT H-2, currently an **accepted tradeoff — not a build task**.

**Required knowledge**

- Files: `sortCentralQueue` + 15-min starvation ceiling; fleet cap vs
  per-project `PROJECT_BUSY` skip; WP2 fairness counters; WP5 burst results.
- Frameworks: SRE Ch.5 fairness; KEDA/HPA resource model (analogy only);
  ATAM tradeoff + ADR.

**Deliverables (only if WP5 shows noisy-neighbour pain)**

1. ADR recording the decision (keep FIFO vs add quota, with the WP5 numbers).
2. If quota: per-project concurrency/share behind a flag, default off or
   conservative; synthetic tests proving the burst scenario that failed WP5
   now passes without starving anyone else.

**Acceptance**

- Either: WP5 shows no pain → ADR "keep FIFO, revisit on evidence", zero
  code. Or: quota implemented, WP5 burst re-run green.
- Explicit NON-goal: do not build this speculatively. AUDIT found no
  correctness failure here.

**Blocked by:** WP5 numbers. Off the critical path — never a launch blocker
unless WP5 makes it one.

**Slice into tickets:** single ticket (ADR first; implementation only if the
ADR requires it).

**Effort signal:** tiny (ADR only) or medium (quota implementation).

---

## WP7 — Runbooks, ADRs, and docs (config-only, last)

**Goal:** lock in everything WPs 1–5 decided so the next operator — and
the next app-dev project — inherits it. Pure config/docs; no behaviour
change. Do last so it documents reality, not intent.

**Required knowledge**

- Outcomes of WP1 (explicit-`projectId` contract), WP3 (unload/delete
  semantics), WP4 (poison ADR), WP5 (SLOs + drill results), WP6 (fairness
  ADR); existing runner README (drain-and-fence description lives here per
  AUDIT §8); WP2 metric dictionary.

**Deliverables**

1. Runner operator runbook: scope-off/on, safe delete ("scope-off → wait
   idle → delete" or the WP3 equivalent), mid-task unload, lease/credential
   recovery, worktree-cap pressure, quarantine handling (WP4).
2. ADR log: queue-fairness (WP6), unload semantics (WP3), shadowing
   (already implemented — record as-is), poison policy (WP4).
3. Past-ADR conformance note: 0009 (claim epochs), 0010 (burn caps), 0012
   (update floor), 0014 (impromptu priority) — still matching (AUDIT §8).
4. Skills matrix (AUDIT §5 table) committed as the per-project skills
   contract; rename-test record (synthetic non-`kainbain` slugs, 187 green)
   filed so Q5 never needs re-proving from scratch.

**Acceptance**

- A new operator can load/unload/delete/scope a project and handle each
  WP5 drill from the runbook alone.
- Zero code change in this WP (docs/config only) — any behaviour gap found
  while writing becomes a new ticket, not scope creep here.

**Blocked by:** WP1 + WP3 + WP4 + WP5 outcomes. Starts last.

**Slice into tickets:** (a) runbook; (b) ADRs + conformance note;
(c) skills contract + rename record. All parallelisable.

**Effort signal:** small. Writing only.

---

## What was deliberately left OUT (no WP)

- **Skills overlay rework (Q6):** AUDIT PASS with 55 + injection + curation
  suites green across shadowed/unshadowed/missing/invalid/oversized cases.
  No WP; the WP7 contract-doc pins the behaviour.
- **Hard-coding purge (Q5):** zero true assumptions found; §4 dispositions
  stand. No WP; WP1's explicit-`projectId` rule prevents the only
  adjacent smell (default-tenant fallback) from becoming one.
- **Switch-without-interruption (Q1) and single-queue collapse (Q2):**
  mechanisms verified + tested (`noDoubleDispatch`, `centralQueueFairness`,
  `scanClaimableTasks`, caps suites). No WP except the conditional WP6.
- **Synthetic-test infrastructure (Q7):** backstop + seams verified working
  (187 green, contamination clean). No WP; every WP above reuses it.

## Suggested ticket order (critical path)

```
WP1 ─┐
WP2 ─┼──▶ WP3 ─┬──▶ WP5 ─▶ WP6? ─▶ WP7
WP4 ─┘         │
     (WP2+WP3+WP4 feed WP5; WP1 gates WP5's validity)
```

Minimum launch sequence for "start developing apps" (AUDIT's small-scale
verdict already covers this): WP1 → WP3 → WP4(ADR) → WP7-runbook-lite.

{"content":"# DELIVERABLES.md — Multi-project production-readiness work packages

Task: `5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085` — make KainBain safe to run
multiple projects on shared runners at production-level workloads.

Source of truth: [AUDIT.md](./AUDIT.md) (verdict: READY WITH HITCHES at
small scale, 2–3 projects / 1–2 runners; production-scale gate open).
Guidance: [FRAMEWORKS.md](./FRAMEWORKS.md). Surveys:
[INTENT-SURVEY.md](./INTENT-SURVEY.md), [FEEDBACK_SURVEY.md](./FEEDBACK_SURVEY.md).

## How to read this file

- Each work package (WP) is a **whole, ticketable step**: one owner, one
  acceptance gate, shippable on its own. Ticket-splitting hints are inside
  each WP ("Slice into tickets").
- Ordering follows **"make the change easy, then make the change"** (Beck
  XP): structural seams and safety rails first (WP1–WP2), behaviour fixes
  next (WP3–WP4), measurement and drills once the signals exist (WP5),
  conditional scale-out only on evidence (WP6), config/docs last (WP7).
- Every WP states its **required knowledge** (files + framework clauses)
  so a ticket implementer never has to re-derive the audit.
- Global constraint on ALL WPs (from the task + AUDIT §6): **no real
  projects**. All verification uses ephemeral temp-dir fixtures
  (`proj-alpha`/`proj-beta`-style) behind `api/testSetup.isolation.js` +
  `api/isolatedTestRoots.js`, with before/after contamination checks on
  `~/projects`, `~/.kainbain/projects.json`, `~/.kainbain/engine/*`.
  Live dummy projects are read-only evidence, never mutation targets.
- Path note: AUDIT.md cites evidence under `/home/[REDACTED]/...`; the live
  checkout root differs but relative paths (`api/...`, `runner/...`,
  `frontend/...`) are identical. Resolve relatively.

## Dependency map

```
WP1 (tenant-safety seam) ──┐
WP2 (observability seam) ───┼──▶ WP5 (SLO gate + failure drills)
WP3 (lifecycle semantics) ──┘         │
WP4 (poison-task policy) ────────────┘
WP6 (fairness quota, CONDITIONAL on WP5 evidence) — standalone, off critical path
WP7 (runbooks/ADRs/docs, config-only) — last, depends on WP1+WP3+WP4+WP5 outcomes
```

- WP5 is blocked on WP1 (correctness must be fenced before load proves
  anything), WP2 (no SLO verdict without the signals), WP3 (unload drill
  needs defined semantics), WP4 (poison drill needs the policy).
- WP6 must NOT start before WP5 has numbers; it is explicitly conditional.
- WP7 is pure config/docs; do it last so it documents what was actually built.

---

## WP1 — Close the cross-project tenant-safety gap (H-1 + H-4)

**Goal:** make cross-project writes structurally impossible on the runner
path, not merely unlikely. Covers AUDIT H-1 (fail-open active-project
fallback) and H-4 (ledger never compares `hold.projectId`).

**Required knowledge**

- Files: `api/projectResolution.js` (`resolveProjectId`, lines ~8–14 —
  the `?? activeProject` fallback); `api/flow/runnerRoutes.js` (`guardedTask`
  ~L510, claim path ~L980, plus `progress`/`logs`/`verify-sha`/
  `complete-execution`/`steer-ack`/`interrupt` and `integration*` routes);
  `api/flow/claimStore.js` (`describe()` ~L230–239 — strips `projectId`);
  `api/flow/executionLedger.js` (`_holdOrThrow` ~L91–103 — checks only
  executionId/epoch/runnerId); `runner/client.js` (all calls already send
  explicit `projectId` — the fix must not break the daemon).
- Frameworks: OWASP ASVS 4.0 V4.1/V5.1 object-level authorisation
  (every `projectId` is a BOLA boundary); ISO 25010 security/integrity.
- Survey anchor: FEEDBACK_SURVEY q5 — true `kainbain`-as-project/default-
  tenant assumptions are **blockers**.

**Deliverables**

1. Explicit-`projectId` enforcement on all runner-mutating routes:
   missing `projectId` → `400` (never active-project fallback). Non-mutating
   UI/view routes may keep the fallback; document the split.
2. `ClaimStore.describe()` includes `projectId`; `_holdOrThrow` (or its
   successor guard) compares request `projectId` against `hold.projectId`
   and rejects mismatches with a named fencing error.
3. Regression tests (synthetic only): omitted-`projectId` → 400 on every
   mutated route; cross-project replay (A's lease against B's task, stale
   epoch, second claimer → `CLAIM_CONFLICT`/`STALE_EPOCH`/404) — extend the
   AUDIT Q4 probe (`/tmp/kb-q4-probe.mjs` pattern) into a committed suite.
4. Brief migration note: any current caller omitting `projectId` (AUDIT says
   none in the daemon — verify) is updated.

**Acceptance**

- Full Q4 matrix green on synthetic fixtures: correct-project writes
  accepted; wrong-project/stale-epoch/double-claim always rejected; no
  fallback-to-active on any mutating route.
- Existing suites still green: `claimStore`, `executionLedger`,
  `runnerPolicyDispatch`, `integrationDispatch`, `projectResolution`.

**Blocks / unblocks:** blocks WP5 (load must run against fenced code).
No dependency on other WPs — do first.

**Slice into tickets:** (a) route-guard + 400 tests; (b) ledger `projectId`
plumbing + fencing tests; (c) caller audit + migration note. (a) and (b) can
parallelise; (c) follows (a).

**Effort signal:** small–medium. Centralised guards, no queue/semantics change.

---

## WP2 — Add the missing production signals (H-5)

**Goal:** make multi-project behaviour *measurable* so the SLO gate (WP5)
can pass or fail honestly. Covers AUDIT H-5. This is the "make the change
easy" seam for everything quantitative.

**Required knowledge**

- Files: `api/watch/observabilityMetrics.js` (existing: `queueDepth`,
  scheduler stats, git contention); ledger `staleRejected` counters;
  `/runners/monitor` live-hold source; dispatch path (`api/flow/dispatch/
  scanClaimableTasks.js`, `api/flow/scheduler/centralQueuePolicy.js`,
  `sortCentralQueue`); fleet cap `429 FLEET_CONCURRENCY_EXHAUSTED` and
  per-project `PROJECT_BUSY` skip paths (new counters hook here).
- Frameworks: SRE Ch.10 / OTel + RED/USE + golden signals (FRAMEWORKS §3.8);
  minimum set per §3.8: dispatch latency, queue depth, claim-fencing
  rejections, per-project throughput/fairness, worktree evictions,
  skill size-cap omissions.

**Deliverables**

1. New counters/histograms: dispatch-latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99),
   per-project claimed/completed throughput + wait-time (feeds fairness),
   claim success rate (non-conflict claims / attempts, excluding operator
   pauses and version refusals), scope/fencing rejection breakdown
   (`PROJECT_SCOPE`, `STALE_EPOCH`, `CLAIM_CONFLICT`).
2. Metrics are per-project labelled and queryable over a load window
   (whatever the existing exposition is — extend it, don't add a second
   system).
3. Unit/integration tests on synthetic fixtures: each new signal moves
   under a scripted scenario (burst → fairness counters diverge correctly;
   conflict → conflict counter increments).
4. One-page metric dictionary (name, labels, what proves what) — feeds WP7.

**Acceptance**

- Every §3.8 minimum signal exists and is observable during a scripted
  synthetic burst; AUDIT's "unmeasured" list for Q8 is empty.
- No live-project writes during verification (contamination check clean).

**Blocks / unblocks:** blocks WP5 (SLOs need these signals). Independent of
WP1/WP3 — can parallelise with WP1.

**Slice into tickets:** (a) latency + queue-depth percentiles; (b) claim/
fencing + scope counters; (c) per-project throughput/fairness + dictionary.
All three can parallelise behind the agreed metric exposition.

**Effort signal:** small–medium. Additive instrumentation, no behaviour change.

---

## WP3 — Define and fence project unload/delete (H-3)

**Goal:** turn unload/delete from "mostly works, with a zombie window"
into a documented, fenced lifecycle. Covers AUDIT H-3 (`DELETE
/projects/:id` is memory-only, unfenced; rescan resurrects; live holds
survive until TTL).

**Required knowledge**

- Files: `api/routes/projects.js` (`DELETE /projects/:id` ~L602);
  `api/projectStore.js` (`deleteProject` ~L2006, rescan logic, first-key
  active default ~L529–530); registry file handling (`api/projectRegistry.js`
  — advisory, missing/corrupt → empty); operator scope path
  (`PATCH /runners/:id/config` `{ projectScope }` via `operatorConfigVerdict`
  — the *already-correct* drain-and-fence reference implementation: future
  matching only, live holds drain); `runner/project.js` workdir hygiene
  (`WORKTREE_CAP`, LRU evict, `kb-recovery/*` parking).
- Frameworks: Twelve-Factor III/IX (config, disposability); Compensating
  Transaction (unload parks + fences + is reversible); ISO 25010
  reliability/recoverability.
- Survey anchor: FEEDBACK_SURVEY q2 — drain-and-fence is the required
  semantic (in-flight finishes or parks, no new claims, re-load clean).

**Deliverables**

1. Decide and implement ONE of: (a) fence holds + remove persisted state
   (registry/config entries) on delete, or (b) keep delete shallow but
   refuse it while holds are live (`409` with active-hold list) and
   document "scope-off → wait idle → delete". AUDIT recommends (a) or the
   documented (b); do not leave the current silent-zombie behaviour.
2. State-transition tests (synthetic): active → scope-off mid-task (no new
   claims, in-flight drains) → delete → rescan does NOT resurrect →
   re-register is clean and idempotent (`registerProjectPath` no-op).
3. Operator error codes for post-unload claims (loud refusal, never silent
   skip — same contract as `PROJECT_SCOPE`).

**Acceptance**

- Mid-task unload/delete drill: zero lost work, zero zombie claims past
  the defined fence, re-load resumes cleanly.
- Advisory-registry contract preserved: corrupt/missing registry still
  degrades to empty, never broken boot.

**Blocks / unblocks:** blocks WP5's unload-mid-task drill. Independent of
WP1/WP2 — can parallelise.

**Slice into tickets:** (a) decision + fence/delete implementation;
(b) state-transition suite; (c) operator error UX. (b) pins (a)'s contract.

**Effort signal:** medium. Lifecycle semantics touch store + registry + routes.

---

## WP4 — Decide the poison-task policy (O-3)

**Goal:** answer AUDIT's open question — what happens to a task that can
never succeed — before it wedges the shared queue in production. Covers
O-3 (quarantine exists for models only; task-level dead-letter unverified).

**Required knowledge**

- Files: stage-failure paths (task fail vs requeue-loop — trace from the
  runner daemon through completion routes); existing model quarantine
  (reuse its shape if suitable); `WORKTREE_CAP` + `kb-recovery/*` parking
  (poison tasks also consume workdirs); WP2 counters (poison retries must
  be visible).
- Frameworks: Poison Pill + Dead-Letter pattern (FRAMEWORKS §3.5); SRE
  Ch.7 overload handling; ISO 25010 fault tolerance.
- Note: AUDIT Q2 backpressure (fleet 429, per-project skip, circuit
  breaker) already bounds *load*; this WP bounds *permanent failure*.

**Deliverables**

1. Policy decision recorded as ADR: retry budget (N attempts) → quarantine/
   dead-letter with reason preserved → queue continues for other projects;
   operator unquarantine path. (If current fail-fast already bounds it,
   the ADR records the proof + test instead of new code.)
2. Implementation if the proof fails: attempt counter, quarantine state,
   per-project quarantine visibility, no requeue-loop.
3. Synthetic tests: always-failing stage/skill/repo task → quarantined
   after N, sibling-project tasks drain unaffected.

**Acceptance**

- One poison task cannot stall the mixed queue; quarantine is observable
  (WP2 signals) and reversible by the operator.
- ADR filed (feeds WP7's tradeoff log).

**Blocks / unblocks:** blocks WP5's poison drill. Independent of WP1–WP3 —
can parallelise once the ADR direction is set.

**Slice into tickets:** (a) failure-path trace + ADR; (b) implementation
(if needed) + tests. (b) is conditional on (a)'s finding.

**Effort signal:** small if fail-fast already bounds it; medium if a
dead-letter store is built. Timebox the trace before committing to a build.

---

## WP5 — Run the production-scale gate: SLOs + load + failure drills (Q8)

**Goal:** close the AUDIT Q8 gate — either prove production-scale
readiness against pre-declared SLOs or produce the bounded failure list.
This WP makes no product change; it renders the verdict WP1–WP4 earned.
Do NOT claim production readiness without it.

**Required knowledge**

- AUDIT §7 proposal (adopt or amend first): correctness 100% (zero
  mis-attributed claims/progress/reports — error-budget-zero); dispatch
  latency p95 < 2 s under the agreed profile (after WP2); claim success
  rate > 99% (excl. operator pauses/version refusals); dispatch-endpoint
  non-5xx > 99.9% over the soak.
- Load profile (synthetic, mock harnesses, REAL dispatch path — never mock
  the queue, Twelve-Factor X parity): steady state (2–3 projects × few
  tasks) → single-project burst (noisy neighbour) → all-project burst →
  sustained queue depth; Little's-law sanity (`L = λW`) on depth.
- Failure drills: runner kill mid-task (lease expiry → re-queue, no
  cross-project loss); backend restart mid-dispatch (holds drop, epochs
  persist, re-queue as interrupted); poison task (WP4 policy); worktree-cap
  pressure (LRU + recovery parking); scope-off unload mid-task (WP3).
- Frameworks: SRE Ch.3/5/17 (SLOs, capacity, readiness checklist); 29119
  load/performance type; Bulkhead/Idempotent-Consumer/Circuit-Breaker
  expectations.

**Deliverables**

1. Agreed SLO set (signed off before the rig runs — SRE Ch.3 rule).
2. Load + drill report: tool + script versions, results vs each SLO,
   Little's-law check, per-drill outcome (recover clean / bounded damage /
   blocker found).
3. Verdict update: production-ready / ready-with-hitches / NOT ready, with
   the failing clause cited; any new blocker gets a WP1–WP4-style follow-up.

**Acceptance**

- SLOs declared BEFORE measurement; all drills executed on synthetic
  fixtures; contamination check clean; report filed in the task docs.
- Q8 exit criteria (FRAMEWORKS §8) all met, or the miss is named.

**Blocked by:** WP1 (fenced code), WP2 (signals), WP3 (unload semantics),
WP4 (poison policy). Starts only when all four land.

**Slice into tickets:** (a) SLO sign-off + rig + steady/burst runs;
(b) failure drills (one ticket per drill is fine — they parallelise);
(c) report + verdict. (a) first, (b) in any order, (c) last.

**Effort signal:** medium. Mostly rig + runs, not product code.

---

## WP6 — Fairness quota, ONLY on WP5 evidence (H-2, conditional)

**Goal:** decide with data whether FIFO-oldest-first + 15-minute ceiling
(`sortCentralQueue` in `api/flow/scheduler/centralQueuePolicy.js`) is
enough, or whether a noisy neighbour needs a per-project quota. Covers
AUDIT H-2, currently an **accepted tradeoff — not a build task**.

**Required knowledge**

- Files: `sortCentralQueue` + 15-min starvation ceiling; fleet cap vs
  per-project `PROJECT_BUSY` skip; WP2 fairness counters; WP5 burst results.
- Frameworks: SRE Ch.5 fairness; KEDA/HPA resource model (analogy only);
  ATAM tradeoff + ADR.

**Deliverables (only if WP5 shows noisy-neighbour pain)**

1. ADR recording the decision (keep FIFO vs add quota, with the WP5 numbers).
2. If quota: per-project concurrency/share behind a flag, default off or
   conservative; synthetic tests proving the burst scenario that failed WP5
   now passes without starving anyone else.

**Acceptance**

- Either: WP5 shows no pain → ADR "keep FIFO, revisit on evidence", zero
  code. Or: quota implemented, WP5 burst re-run green.
- Explicit NON-goal: do not build this speculatively. AUDIT found no
  correctness failure here.

**Blocked by:** WP5 numbers. Off the critical path — never a launch blocker
unless WP5 makes it one.

**Slice into tickets:** single ticket (ADR first; implementation only if the
ADR requires it).

**Effort signal:** tiny (ADR only) or medium (quota implementation).

---

## WP7 — Runbooks, ADRs, and docs (config-only, last)

**Goal:** lock in everything WPs 1–5 decided so the next operator — and
the next app-dev project — inherits it. Pure config/docs; no behaviour
change. Do last so it documents reality, not intent.

**Required knowledge**

- Outcomes of WP1 (explicit-`projectId` contract), WP3 (unload/delete
  semantics), WP4 (poison ADR), WP5 (SLOs + drill results), WP6 (fairness
  ADR); existing runner README (drain-and-fence description lives here per
  AUDIT §8); WP2 metric dictionary.

**Deliverables**

1. Runner operator runbook: scope-off/on, safe delete ("scope-off → wait
   idle → delete" or the WP3 equivalent), mid-task unload, lease/credential
   recovery, worktree-cap pressure, quarantine handling (WP4).
2. ADR log: queue-fairness (WP6), unload semantics (WP3), shadowing
   (already implemented — record as-is), poison policy (WP4).
3. Past-ADR conformance note: 0009 (claim epochs), 0010 (burn caps), 0012
   (update floor), 0014 (impromptu priority) — still matching (AUDIT §8).
4. Skills matrix (AUDIT §5 table) committed as the per-project skills
   contract; rename-test record (synthetic non-`kainbain` slugs, 187 green)
   filed so Q5 never needs re-proving from scratch.

**Acceptance**

- A new operator can load/unload/delete/scope a project and handle each
  WP5 drill from the runbook alone.
- Zero code change in this WP (docs/config only) — any behaviour gap found
  while writing becomes a new ticket, not scope creep here.

**Blocked by:** WP1 + WP3 + WP4 + WP5 outcomes. Starts last.

**Slice into tickets:** (a) runbook; (b) ADRs + conformance note;
(c) skills contract + rename record. All parallelisable.

**Effort signal:** small. Writing only.

---

## What was deliberately left OUT (no WP)

- **Skills overlay rework (Q6):** AUDIT PASS with 55 + injection + curation
  suites green across shadowed/unshadowed/missing/invalid/oversized cases.
  No WP; the WP7 contract-doc pins the behaviour.
- **Hard-coding purge (Q5):** zero true assumptions found; §4 dispositions
  stand. No WP; WP1's explicit-`projectId` rule prevents the only
  adjacent smell (default-tenant fallback) from becoming one.
- **Switch-without-interruption (Q1) and single-queue collapse (Q2):**
  mechanisms verified + tested (`noDoubleDispatch`, `centralQueueFairness`,
  `scanClaimableTasks`, caps suites). No WP except the conditional WP6.
- **Synthetic-test infrastructure (Q7):** backstop + seams verified working
  (187 green, contamination clean). No WP; every WP above reuses it.

## Suggested ticket order (critical path)

```
WP1 ─┐
WP2 ─┼──▶ WP3 ─┬──▶ WP5 ─▶ WP6? ─▶ WP7
WP4 ─┘         │
     (WP2+WP3+WP4 feed WP5; WP1 gates WP5's validity)
```

Minimum launch sequence for "start developing apps" (AUDIT's small-scale
verdict already covers this): WP1 → WP3 → WP4(ADR) → WP7-runbook-lite.
Full production-scale claim additionally requires WP2 → WP5, with WP6 only
on WP5 evidence.

11|## How to read this file
12|
13|- Each work package (WP) is a **whole, ticketable step**: one owner, one
14|  acceptance gate, shippable on its own. Ticket-splitting hints are inside
15|  each WP ("Slice into tickets").
16|- Ordering follows **"make the change easy, then make the change"** (Beck
17|  XP): structural seams and safety rails first (WP1–WP2), behaviour fixes
18|  next (WP3–WP4), measurement and drills once the signals exist (WP5),
19|  conditional scale-out only on evidence (WP6), config/docs last (WP7).
20|- Every WP states its **required knowledge** (files + framework clauses)
21|  so a ticket implementer never has to re-derive the audit.
22|- Global constraint on ALL WPs (from the task + AUDIT §6): **no real
23|  projects**. All verification uses ephemeral temp-dir fixtures
24|  (`proj-alpha`/`proj-beta`-style) behind `api/testSetup.isolation.js` +
25|  `api/isolatedTestRoots.js`, with before/after contamination checks on
26|  `~/projects`, `~/.kainbain/projects.json`, `~/.kainbain/engine/*`.
27|  Live dummy projects are read-only evidence, never mutation targets.
28|- Path note: AUDIT.md cites evidence under `/home/[REDACTED]/...`; the live
29|  checkout root differs but relative paths (`api/...`, `runner/...`,
30|  `frontend/...`) are identical. Resolve relatively.

32|## Dependency map
33|
34|```
35|WP1 (tenant-safety seam) ──┐
36|WP2 (observability seam) ───┼──▶ WP5 (SLO gate + failure drills)
37|WP3 (lifecycle semantics) ──┘         │
38|WP4 (poison-task policy) ────────────┘
39|WP6 (fairness quota, CONDITIONAL on WP5 evidence) — standalone, off critical path
40|WP7 (runbooks/ADRs/docs, config-only) — last, depends on WP1+WP3+WP4+WP5 outcomes
41|```
42|
43|- WP5 is blocked on WP1 (correctness must be fenced before load proves
44|  anything), WP2 (no SLO verdict without the signals), WP3 (unload drill
45|  needs defined semantics), WP4 (poison drill needs the policy).
46|- WP6 must NOT start before WP5 has numbers; it is explicitly conditional.
47|- WP7 is pure config/docs; do it last so it documents what was actually built.

51|## WP1 — Close the cross-project tenant-safety gap (H-1 + H-4)
52|
53|**Goal:** make cross-project writes structurally impossible on the runner
54|path, not merely unlikely. Covers AUDIT H-1 (fail-open active-project
55|fallback) and H-4 (ledger never compares `hold.projectId`).
56|
57|**Required knowledge**
58|
59|- Files: `api/projectResolution.js` (`resolveProjectId`, lines ~8–14 —
60|  the `?? activeProject` fallback); `api/flow/runnerRoutes.js` (`guardedTask`
61|  ~L510, claim path ~L980, plus `progress`/`logs`/`verify-sha`/
62|  `complete-execution`/`steer-ack`/`interrupt` and `integration*` routes);
63|  `api/flow/claimStore.js` (`describe()` ~L230–239 — strips `projectId`);
64|  `api/flow/executionLedger.js` (`_holdOrThrow` ~L91–103 — checks only
65|  executionId/epoch/runnerId); `runner/client.js` (all calls already send
66|  explicit `projectId` — the fix must not break the daemon).
67|- Frameworks: OWASP ASVS 4.0 V4.1/V5.1 object-level authorisation
68|  (every `projectId` is a BOLA boundary); ISO 25010 security/integrity.
69|- Survey anchor: FEEDBACK_SURVEY q5 — true `kainbain`-as-project/default-
70|  tenant assumptions are **blockers**.
71|
72|**Deliverables**
73|
74|1. Explicit-`projectId` enforcement on all runner-mutating routes:
75|   missing `projectId` → `400` (never active-project fallback). Non-mutating
76|   UI/view routes may keep the fallback; document the split.
77|2. `ClaimStore.describe()` includes `projectId`; `_holdOrThrow` (or its
78|   successor guard) compares request `projectId` against `hold.projectId`
79|   and rejects mismatches with a named fencing error.
80|3. Regression tests (synthetic only): omitted-`projectId` → 400 on every
81|   mutated route; cross-project replay (A's lease against B's task, stale
82|   epoch, second claimer → `CLAIM_CONFLICT`/`STALE_EPOCH`/404) — extend the
83|   AUDIT Q4 probe (`/tmp/kb-q4-probe.mjs` pattern) into a committed suite.
84|4. Brief migration note: any current caller omitting `projectId` (AUDIT says
85|   none in the daemon — verify) is updated.
86|
87|**Acceptance**
88|
89|- Full Q4 matrix green on synthetic fixtures: correct-project writes
90|  accepted; wrong-project/stale-epoch/double-claim always rejected; no
91|  fallback-to-active on any mutating route.
92|- Existing suites still green: `claimStore`, `executionLedger`,
93|  `runnerPolicyDispatch`, `integrationDispatch`, `projectResolution`.
94|
95|**Blocks / unblocks:** blocks WP5 (load must run against fenced code).
96|No dependency on other WPs — do first.
97|
98|**Slice into tickets:** (a) route-guard + 400 tests; (b) ledger `projectId`
99|plumbing + fencing tests; (c) caller audit + migration note. (a) and (b) can
100|parallelise; (c) follows (a).
101|
102|**Effort signal:** small–medium. Centralised guards, no queue/semantics change.

106|## WP2 — Add the missing production signals (H-5)
107|
108|**Goal:** make multi-project behaviour *measurable* so the SLO gate (WP5)
109|can pass or fail honestly. Covers AUDIT H-5. This is the "make the change
110|easy" seam for everything quantitative.
111|
112|**Required knowledge**
113|
114|- Files: `api/watch/observabilityMetrics.js` (existing: `queueDepth`,
115|  scheduler stats, git contention); ledger `staleRejected` counters;
116|  `/runners/monitor` live-hold source; dispatch path (`api/flow/dispatch/
117|  scanClaimableTasks.js`, `api/flow/scheduler/centralQueuePolicy.js`,
118|  `sortCentralQueue`); fleet cap `429 FLEET_CONCURRENCY_EXHAUSTED` and
119|  per-project `PROJECT_BUSY` skip paths (new counters hook here).
120|- Frameworks: SRE Ch.10 / OTel + RED/USE + golden signals (FRAMEWORKS §3.8);
121|  minimum set per §3.8: dispatch latency, queue depth, claim-fencing
122|  rejections, per-project throughput/fairness, worktree evictions,
123|  skill size-cap omissions.
124|
125|**Deliverables**
126|
127|1. New counters/histograms: dispatch-latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99),
128|   per-project claimed/completed throughput + wait-time (feeds fairness),
129|   claim success rate (non-conflict claims / attempts, excluding operator
130|   pauses and version refusals), scope/fencing rejection breakdown
131|   (`PROJECT_SCOPE`, `STALE_EPOCH`, `CLAIM_CONFLICT`).
132|2. Metrics are per-project labelled and queryable over a load window
133|   (whatever the existing exposition is — extend it, don't add a second
134|   system).
135|3. Unit/integration tests on synthetic fixtures: each new signal moves
136|   under a scripted scenario (burst → fairness counters diverge correctly;
137|   conflict → conflict counter increments).
138|4. One-page metric dictionary (name, labels, what proves what) — feeds WP7.
139|
140|**Acceptance**
141|
142|- Every §3.8 minimum signal exists and is observable during a scripted
143|  synthetic burst; AUDIT's "unmeasured" list for Q8 is empty.
144|- No live-project writes during verification (contamination check clean).

146|**Blocks / unblocks:** blocks WP5 (SLOs need these signals). Independent of
147|WP1/WP3 — can parallelise with WP1.
148|
149|**Slice into tickets:** (a) latency + queue-depth percentiles; (b) claim/
150|fencing + scope counters; (c) per-project throughput/fairness + dictionary.

153|**Effort signal:** small–medium. Additive instrumentation, no behaviour change.

157|## WP3 — Define and fence project unload/delete (H-3)
158|
159|**Goal:** turn unload/delete from "mostly works, with a zombie window"
160|into a documented, fenced lifecycle. Covers AUDIT H-3 (`DELETE
161|/projects/:id` is memory-only, unfenced; rescan resurrects; live holds
162|survive until TTL).
163|
164|**Required knowledge**
165|
166|- Files: `api/routes/projects.js` (`DELETE /projects/:id` ~L602);
167|  `api/projectStore.js` (`deleteProject` ~L2006, rescan logic, first-key
168|  active default ~L529–530); registry file handling (`api/projectRegistry.js`
169|  — advisory, missing/corrupt → empty); operator scope path
170|  (`PATCH /runners/:id/config` `{ projectScope }` via `operatorConfigVerdict`
171|  — the *already-correct* drain-and-fence reference implementation: future
172|  matching only, live holds drain); `runner/project.js` workdir hygiene
173|  (`WORKTREE_CAP`, LRU evict, `kb-recovery/*` parking).
174|- Frameworks: Twelve-Factor III/IX (config, disposability); Compensating
175|  Transaction (unload parks + fences + is reversible); ISO 25010
176|  reliability/recoverability.
177|- Survey anchor: FEEDBACK_SURVEY q2 — drain-and-fence is the required
178|  semantic (in-flight finishes or parks, no new claims, re-load clean).
179|
180|**Deliverables**
181|
182|1. Decide and implement ONE of: (a) fence holds + remove persisted state
183|   (registry/config entries) on delete, or (b) keep delete shallow but
184|   refuse it while holds are live (`409` with active-hold list) and
185|   document "scope-off → wait idle → delete". AUDIT recommends (a) or the
186|   documented (b); do not leave the current silent-zombie behaviour.
187|2. State-transition tests (synthetic): active → scope-off mid-task (no new
188|   claims, in-flight drains) → delete → rescan does NOT resurrect →
189|   re-register is clean and idempotent (`registerProjectPath` no-op).
190|3. Operator error codes for post-unload claims (loud refusal, never silent
191|   skip — same contract as `PROJECT_SCOPE`).
192|
193|**Acceptance**
194|
195|- Mid-task unload/delete drill: zero lost work, zero zombie claims past
196|  the defined fence, re-load resumes cleanly.
197|- Advisory-registry contract preserved: corrupt/missing registry still
198|  degrades to empty, never broken boot.
199|
200|**Blocks / unblocks:** blocks WP5's unload-mid-task drill. Independent of
201|WP1/WP2 — can parallelise.
202|
203|**Slice into tickets:** (a) decision + fence/delete implementation;
204|(b) state-transition suite; (c) operator error UX. (b) pins (a)'s contract.
205|
206|**Effort signal:** medium. Lifecycle semantics touch store + registry + routes.
207|
