210|## WP4 — Decide the poison-task policy (O-3)
211|
212|**Goal:** answer AUDIT's open question — what happens to a task that can
213|never succeed — before it wedges the shared queue in production. Covers
214|O-3 (quarantine exists for models only; task-level dead-letter unverified).
215|
216|**Required knowledge**
217|
218|- Files: stage-failure paths (task fail vs requeue-loop — trace from the
219|  runner daemon through completion routes); existing model quarantine
220|  (reuse its shape if suitable); `WORKTREE_CAP` + `kb-recovery/*` parking
221|  (poison tasks also consume workdirs); WP2 counters (poison retries must
222|  be visible).
223|- Frameworks: Poison Pill + Dead-Letter pattern (FRAMEWORKS §3.5); SRE
224|  Ch.7 overload handling; ISO 25010 fault tolerance.
225|- Note: AUDIT Q2 backpressure (fleet 429, per-project skip, circuit
226|  breaker) already bounds *load*; this WP bounds *permanent failure*.
227|
228|**Deliverables**
229|
230|1. Policy decision recorded as ADR: retry budget (N attempts) → quarantine/
231|   dead-letter with reason preserved → queue continues for other projects;
232|   operator unquarantine path. (If current fail-fast already bounds it,
233|   the ADR records the proof + test instead of new code.)
234|2. Implementation if the proof fails: attempt counter, quarantine state,
235|   per-project quarantine visibility, no requeue-loop.
236|3. Synthetic tests: always-failing stage/skill/repo task → quarantined
237|   after N, sibling-project tasks drain unaffected.
238|
239|**Acceptance**
240|
241|- One poison task cannot stall the mixed queue; quarantine is observable
242|  (WP2 signals) and reversible by the operator.
243|- ADR filed (feeds WP7's tradeoff log).
244|
245|**Blocks / unblocks:** blocks WP5's poison drill. Independent of WP1–WP3 —
246|can parallelise once the ADR direction is set.
247|
248|**Slice into tickets:** (a) failure-path trace + ADR; (b) implementation
249|(if needed) + tests. (b) is conditional on (a)'s finding.
250|
251|**Effort signal:** small if fail-fast already bounds it; medium if a
252|dead-letter store is built. Timebox the trace before committing to a build.
253|
254|---
255|
256|## WP5 — Run the production-scale gate: SLOs + load + failure drills (Q8)
257|
258|**Goal:** close the AUDIT Q8 gate — either prove production-scale
259|readiness against pre-declared SLOs or produce the bounded failure list.
260|This WP makes no product change; it renders the verdict WP1–WP4 earned.
261|Do NOT claim production readiness without it.
262|
263|**Required knowledge**
264|
265|- AUDIT §7 proposal (adopt or amend first): correctness 100% (zero
266|  mis-attributed claims/progress/reports — error-budget-zero); dispatch
267|  latency p95 < 2 s under the agreed profile (after WP2); claim success
268|  rate > 99% (excl. operator pauses/version refusals); dispatch-endpoint
269|  non-5xx > 99.9% over the soak.
270|- Load profile (synthetic, mock harnesses, REAL dispatch path — never mock
271|  the queue, Twelve-Factor X parity): steady state (2–3 projects × few
272|  tasks) → single-project burst (noisy neighbour) → all-project burst →
273|  sustained queue depth; Little's-law sanity (`L = λW`) on depth.
274|- Failure drills: runner kill mid-task (lease expiry → re-queue, no
275|  cross-project loss); backend restart mid-dispatch (holds drop, epochs
276|  persist, re-queue as interrupted); poison task (WP4 policy); worktree-cap
277|  pressure (LRU + recovery parking); scope-off unload mid-task (WP3).
278|- Frameworks: SRE Ch.3/5/17 (SLOs, capacity, readiness checklist); 29119
279|  load/performance type; Bulkhead/Idempotent-Consumer/Circuit-Breaker
280|  expectations.
281|
282|**Deliverables**
283|
284|1. Agreed SLO set (signed off before the rig runs — SRE Ch.3 rule).
285|2. Load + drill report: tool + script versions, results vs each SLO,
286|   Little's-law check, per-drill outcome (recover clean / bounded damage /
287|   blocker found).
288|3. Verdict update: production-ready / ready-with-hitches / NOT ready, with
289|   the failing clause cited; any new blocker gets a WP1–WP4-style follow-up.
290|
291|**Acceptance**
292|
293|- SLOs declared BEFORE measurement; all drills executed on synthetic
294|  fixtures; contamination check clean; report filed in the task docs.
295|- Q8 exit criteria (FRAMEWORKS §8) all met, or the miss is named.
296|
297|**Blocked by:** WP1 (fenced code), WP2 (signals), WP3 (unload semantics),
298|WP4 (poison policy). Starts only when all four land.
299|
300|**Slice into tickets:** (a) SLO sign-off + rig + steady/burst runs;
301|(b) failure drills (one ticket per drill is fine — they parallelise);
302|(c) report + verdict. (a) first, (b) in any order, (c) last.
303|
304|**Effort signal:** medium. Mostly rig + runs, not product code.
305|
306|---
307|
308|## WP6 — Fairness quota, ONLY on WP5 evidence (H-2, conditional)
309|
310|**Goal:** decide with data whether FIFO-oldest-first + 15-minute ceiling
311|(`sortCentralQueue` in `api/flow/scheduler/centralQueuePolicy.js`) is
312|enough, or whether a noisy neighbour needs a per-project quota. Covers
313|AUDIT H-2, currently an **accepted tradeoff — not a build task**.
314|
315|**Required knowledge**
316|
317|- Files: `sortCentralQueue` + 15-min starvation ceiling; fleet cap vs
318|  per-project `PROJECT_BUSY` skip; WP2 fairness counters; WP5 burst results.
319|- Frameworks: SRE Ch.5 fairness; KEDA/HPA resource model (analogy only);
320|  ATAM tradeoff + ADR.
321|
322|**Deliverables (only if WP5 shows noisy-neighbour pain)**
323|
324|1. ADR recording the decision (keep FIFO vs add quota, with the WP5 numbers).
325|2. If quota: per-project concurrency/share behind a flag, default off or
326|   conservative; synthetic tests proving the burst scenario that failed WP5
327|   now passes without starving anyone else.
328|
329|**Acceptance**
330|
331|- Either: WP5 shows no pain → ADR "keep FIFO, revisit on evidence", zero
332|  code. Or: quota implemented, WP5 burst re-run green.
333|- Explicit NON-goal: do not build this speculatively. AUDIT found no
334|  correctness failure here.
335|
336|**Blocked by:** WP5 numbers. Off the critical path — never a launch blocker
337|unless WP5 makes it one.
338|
339|**Slice into tickets:** single ticket (ADR first; implementation only if the
340|ADR requires it).
341|
342|**Effort signal:** tiny (ADR only) or medium (quota implementation).
343|
344|---
345|
346|## WP7 — Runbooks, ADRs, and docs (config-only, last)
347|
348|**Goal:** lock in everything WPs 1–5 decided so the next operator — and
349|the next app-dev project — inherits it. Pure config/docs; no behaviour
350|change. Do last so it documents reality, not intent.
351|
352|**Required knowledge**
353|
354|- Outcomes of WP1 (explicit-`projectId` contract), WP3 (unload/delete
355|  semantics), WP4 (poison ADR), WP5 (SLOs + drill results), WP6 (fairness
356|  ADR); existing runner README (drain-and-fence description lives here per
357|  AUDIT §8); WP2 metric dictionary.
358|
359|**Deliverables**
360|
361|1. Runner operator runbook: scope-off/on, safe delete ("scope-off → wait
362|   idle → delete" or the WP3 equivalent), mid-task unload, lease/credential
363|   recovery, worktree-cap pressure, quarantine handling (WP4).
364|2. ADR log: queue-fairness (WP6), unload semantics (WP3), shadowing
365|   (already implemented — record as-is), poison policy (WP4).
366|3. Past-ADR conformance note: 0009 (claim epochs), 0010 (burn caps), 0012
367|   (update floor), 0014 (impromptu priority) — still matching (AUDIT §8).
368|4. Skills matrix (AUDIT §5 table) committed as the per-project skills
369|   contract; rename-test record (synthetic non-`kainbain` slugs, 187 green)
370|   filed so Q5 never needs re-proving from scratch.
371|
372|**Acceptance**
373|
374|- A new operator can load/unload/delete/scope a project and handle each
375|  WP5 drill from the runbook alone.
376|- Zero code change in this WP (docs/config only) — any behaviour gap found
377|  while writing becomes a new ticket, not scope creep here.
378|
379|**Blocked by:** WP1 + WP3 + WP4 + WP5 outcomes. Starts last.
380|
381|**Slice into tickets:** (a) runbook; (b) ADRs + conformance note;
382|(c) skills contract + rename record. All parallelisable.
383|
384|**Effort signal:** small. Writing only.
385|
386|---
387|
388|## What was deliberately left OUT (no WP)
389|
390|- **Skills overlay rework (Q6):** AUDIT PASS with 55 + injection + curation
391|  suites green across shadowed/unshadowed/missing/invalid/oversized cases.
392|  No WP; the WP7 contract-doc pins the behaviour.
393|- **Hard-coding purge (Q5):** zero true assumptions found; §4 dispositions
394|  stand. No WP; WP1's explicit-`projectId` rule prevents the only
395|  adjacent smell (default-tenant fallback) from becoming one.
396|- **Switch-without-interruption (Q1) and single-queue collapse (Q2):**
397|  mechanisms verified + tested (`noDoubleDispatch`, `centralQueueFairness`,
398|  `scanClaimableTasks`, caps suites). No WP except the conditional WP6.
399|- **Synthetic-test infrastructure (Q7):** backstop + seams verified working
400|  (187 green, contamination clean). No WP; every WP above reuses it.
401|
402|## Suggested ticket order (critical path)
403|
404|```
405|WP1 ─┐
406|WP2 ─┼──▶ WP3 ─┬──▶ WP5 ─▶ WP6? ─▶ WP7
407|WP4 ─┘         │
408|     (WP2+WP3+WP4 feed WP5; WP1 gates WP5's validity)
409|```
410|
411|Minimum launch sequence for "start developing apps" (AUDIT's small-scale
412|verdict already covers this): WP1 → WP3 → WP4(ADR) → WP7-runbook-lite.
413|Full production-scale claim additionally requires WP2 → WP5, with WP6 only
414|on WP5 evidence.
